Scope: user request — "run the app in a live emulation, verify every feature works, then
reverse the actual macOS ZCode app (REA) and document everything missing or weaker vs it,
so the Android app is on par or better."

`/Applications/ZCode.app` (asar sha256 `99e280fb90b626cc…`, ~327 MB, out/main+host+renderer
bundles; desktop source reference clone v3.14.3 at `~/Desktop/DEVPROJECTS/zcode/repo`).

Evidence: 76 screenshots `/tmp/walk/*.png` (emulator session), mock relay wire log
`/tmp/mock-relay.log` (v4call receipts), app logcat (`ZCODE-PAIR` tag), REA analysis
`/tmp/zcode-asar-summary.json` (Evidence `agm_27661707668b570e42e5d2ec94b159caa023379929d90e7cb7b882ad0fc9af2a`).

### Defects found in the app (this walk)

- **GAP-A1 (feature break, P1): the workspace hook-trust review card does not exist.**
  ADR-024 landed only half: the domain decode (`SessionState.kt:246,344`), the four v4
  commands (`ConversationPort.kt:270-284`) and the VM verbs (`ConversationViewModel.kt:684-708`)
  all exist, but no composable renders `PendingInteraction.Kind.WORKSPACE_HOOK_REVIEW`, and
  `InteractionCoordinator.reconcileFromSessionState` deliberately parks hook reviews in the
  "counted, no card — INV-14" branch (`InteractionCoordinator.kt:730-733`). Live proof: with
  `MOCK_HOOKS=1` scripting a 3-item review (2 pending + 1 trusted), NO card renders anywhere —
  a session blocking on hook trust has no phone remedy, the exact failure ADR-024 set out to
  close. The ADR's own UX contract (per-item opt-in checkboxes default-off, "Trust N selected
  hooks" disabled at N=0, confirm sheet) is nowhere implemented. Zero UI callers exist for
  trustHooks/revokeHooks/toggleHookItem/grantHookTrust.
- **GAP-A2 (defect, P1): the Approvals inbox never clears answered/resolved interactions.**
  Answered the question from the conversation card (wire ok, state patch `pendingInteractions:[]`
  received — the pinned card cleared) and "Allow once" from the inbox (app log
  `approvals.answer :: interaction=mock-approva option=allowOnce`, mock command id=137): both
  inbox entries remained open through screen re-entry minutes later. `observeOpen` filters
  `resolvedAtMs IS NULL` (`Daos.kt:110`) — the coordinator never marks these records resolved
  (no `interaction.*` warnings in logcat; `v4.call ok in 84ms`). Affects both the state-plane
  and the row-anchored permission classes; the inbox count/badge stays wrong too.
- **GAP-A3 (hygiene, P3): conversations are never unsubscribed.** The host serves
  `unsubscribeConversationV4`/`unsubscribeWorkspaceConfigV4` (extracted host surface,
  `/tmp/host-v4-all.txt`); the phone has no call site anywhere (`app/src/main`,
  `data/src/main`, `core/transport/src/main`). Switching tasks leaves old session
  subscriptions armed on the host — wasted frames to the phone and stale-stream risk after
  reconnects.
- **GAP-A4 (UX, P3): the workflow Run… sheet's Run button is covered by the keyboard** while
  the arg field is focused (observed on device; the tap at the button's AX bounds lands on the
  keyboard). Dismissing the keyboard first works. `imePadding()`/pan behavior for that sheet.
- **GAP-A5 (ANR, P2): "Copy diagnostics to clipboard" can ANR the app.** Reproduced live with
  a full system ANR (`Input dispatching timed out … Waited 5006ms`), trace at
  `/tmp/walk/anr-trace.txt`: `SettingsScreenKt$copyDiagnostics$1$1.invokeSuspend(SettingsScreen.kt:518)`
  calls `ClipboardManager.setPrimaryClip` — a **synchronous binder IPC** — resumed on the Main
  dispatcher; the system clipboard service stalled >5 s and input dispatch timed out. The vc18
  fix moved the REPORT build off-main and the vc20 fix bounded the payload, but the clipboard
  call itself still runs on Main. Fix: hop the `setPrimaryClip` (+ toast) to `Dispatchers.IO`/
  `Default` — clipboard writes are legal from any thread.

## Part B — macOS desktop vs Android companion (REA + source cross-check)

Method: REA `analyze_javascript_application` on the shipped asar (record-and-continue for the
post-signing `pty.node` integrity note), then direct enumeration of the extracted
`out/host/*.js` v4 dispatch surface (`/tmp/host-v4-all.txt`, 37 methods), the desktop source
command registry (`packages/shared/src/zcode-protocol-v4/command.ts`, 34 command types), and
the desktop v4 UI file inventory (`packages/ui/src/v4/`, ~160 files). Cross-checked against
the phone's `core/transport/V4Plane.kt` + `data/session/AgentFacadeClient.kt` +
`data/session/CommandCoordinator.kt` + feature modules, and the Part A device walk.

### B1. Protocol plane parity — VERIFIED AT PARITY

The phone's facade covers the complete host conversation-plane: hello/initialize/subscribe/
resync (conversation, workspace-config), rowsRange, file changes, sendConversationCommand,
attachment upload (begin/chunk/commit/abort/read). Command types: the phone sends 28 of the
desktop's 34; the protocol module (`V4Command.kt`) models all 34.

### B2. Feature gaps (desktop has it, the phone doesn't)

Ordered by user impact. "Modeled" = in `V4Command.kt` but never sent by any coordinator/port.

| # | Gap | Desktop evidence | Phone state | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G1 | **Hook-trust review card** — the desktop shows the blocking review (banner + details + trust flow); the phone renders nothing | `WorkspaceHookPendingBanner.tsx`, `ConversationHookDetailsAction.tsx`, ADR-024 UX contract | GAP-A1 above; wire+VM ready, zero UI | **P1** |
| G2 | **Approvals resolution bookkeeping** — desktop resolves cleanly | interaction auto-resolution family (`useTaskInteractionAutoResolutionSnooze`, `interactionAutoResolutionCommand.ts`) | GAP-A2 above | **P1** |
| G3 | **Workflow run Resume + run-settings amend** — desktop can resume a resumable run and amend run settings | `resumeWorkflowRun`, `amendWorkflowRunSettings` in command.ts; `workflowResumeGate.ts` | Modeled, never sent; run sheet has no Resume/settings actions | P2 |
| G4 | **Queue item delete** — desktop `deleteQueueItem` | command.ts | Modeled, never sent; phone queue has move/edit/send-now/auto-drain/follow-up only | P2 |
| G5 | **Find in conversation** — timeline find with highlight (`conversationFindHighlightDom`, `useConversationTimelineFind`, `conversationFindIndex`) | desktop v4 UI | Absent on phone (trajectory search only covers model calls) | P2 |
| G6 | **Interaction snooze (auto-resolution)** — desktop `snoozeInteractionAutoResolution` + per-task snooze | `useTaskInteractionAutoResolutionSnooze.ts` | Modeled, never sent | P3 |
| G7 | **Selection actions** — text-selection tooltip/menu in the timeline (copy / selection side session / share selection) | `SelectionActionMenu.tsx`, `MarkdownSelectionTooltip.tsx` | Absent | P3 |
| G8 | **Selection side session** — run a selection in a child session | `createSelectionSideSession` in command.ts | Modeled, never sent | P3 |
| G9 | **Shared-context handover** — share/import conversation context refs (`context_refs` on sendText, `discardSharedContext`, `sharedContext*.ts`) | command.ts | Not modeled at all; composer sends no `context_refs` | P3 |
| G10 | **Suggested prompts on the draft screen** — desktop empty-state suggested prompts with rotation + prefill | `featureSuggestedPrompts.ts`, `draftSuggestedPrompt*.ts` | Absent (draft screen is bare) | P3 |
| G11 | **In-conversation quota banner** — desktop warns when the plan bucket runs low mid-session | `ConversationQuotaBanner.tsx`, `sessionQuotaBannerState.ts`, `startPlanQuotaBuckets.ts` | Phone has the Settings quota section (ADR-020) but no live banner | P3 |
| G12 | **Pending-command recovery banner** — desktop surfaces replayable/failed pending commands | `PendingCommandRecoveryBanner.tsx`, `pendingCommandReplay.ts` | Phone has the outbox + journal machinery but no user-facing banner | P3 |
| G13 | **Sessions-index live plane** — desktop subscribes/resyncs the sessions index (cross-session live activity, row activity states) | `subscribeSessionsIndexV4` family, `sessionsIndexStore.ts`, `taskListRowActivity.ts` | Phone polls/refreshes per-screen instead; no live cross-session feed | P3 |
| G14 | **Conversation subscription lifecycle** — desktop unsubscribes conversations/workspace-config on exit | `unsubscribe*V4` in host dispatch | GAP-A3 above | P3 |
| G15 | **Background bash output viewer** — desktop can read background shell output | `backgroundBashOutputV4` | Not consumed by the phone | P3 |
| G16 | **Attachment preview source** — desktop fetches larger/preview attachment renders | `attachmentPreviewSourceV4`, `conversationAttachmentRead/Stat` | Phone uses `attachmentRead` only (smaller previews) | P4 |
| G17 | **Assistant preview cards for rows** — desktop renders artifact preview cards with pptx auto-open | `useAssistantPreviewCardsForRow.ts`, `assistantPreviewPptxAutoOpen.ts` | Phone has `GeneratedArtifactPreview` (narrower: generated-artifact preview only) | P4 |
| G18 | **CUA (computer-use) row groups + permission schema** — desktop groups CUA tool calls, has a dedicated permission plane | `conversationCuaGroups.ts`, `cuaPermission.ts`, zcode-cua package | Phone renders generic tool groups; no CUA-specific grouping/permission copy | P4 |
| G19 | **Conversation share modes** — desktop shares a selection as a link/read-only timeline with preflight; phone shares the transcript text only | `ConversationShare*` family (13 files) | Phone `conv_share` (transcript export) | P4 |

### B3. Deliberate read-only/companion boundaries (NOT gaps — by design, per ADRs/INV)

- Files browser read-only; Git panel bounded to the ADR-021 mutation set; terminal strictly
  view-only (ADR-022); plugins/skills/MCP read-only viewers (INV-9); workflow authoring stays
  desktop-side; hooks configuration desktop-side (the phone only answers trust reviews —
  which is G1); CUA/IDE workbench panes are desktop form-factor. The phone's automations
  surface is FULL parity (create/edit/restart/run-now/delete wired end-to-end; the mock's
  fault message this round was a rig limitation, not an app gate).

### B4. Where the phone is BETTER than the desktop

- Push-style awareness without a push service: approval/task-finished/connection-lost
  notifications + privacy-preserving Minimal detail, live-connection window, auto-reconnect
  checks, Pending-Approvals glance widget, app shortcuts.
- Voice input (ADR-019) in the composer.
- In-app update path with signed release meta (ReleaseParser fails closed) — verified live by
  Ernest in the field (1.2.5→1.2.6).
- Diagnostics export/copy/marker designed for redaction (no conversation content).
- Multi-endpoint (relay QR pairing + direct-server endpoints) with sealed credentials;
  offline queueing with CAS-guarded retries (desktop relies on its local session).
- Dark/light theme override with instant application and system-bar contrast handling.

## Part C — remediation roadmap (recommended order)

1. **Fix round A (P1/P2 defects):**
   - Build the hook-trust review card (ADR-024 contract: per-item opt-in default-off,
     Trust N disabled at 0, confirm sheet, stale_digest state, trust/revoke/toggle wiring
     already in the VM), with a coordinator branch that routes WORKSPACE_HOOK_REVIEW
     interactions into the pinned-card plane; mock rig legs already script the review.
   - Fix approvals resolution: mark repository records resolved on the acknowledge path AND
     on the state-plane disappearance reconciliation for row-anchored machines; add pins for
     inbox-clears-on-answer (state-plane + row-anchored classes).
   - GAP-A5: move the diagnostics clipboard write (and toast) off the Main dispatcher
     (`SettingsScreen.kt:518`) — one-line coroutines fix, ANR eliminated by construction;
     pin with a Robolectric test that the clipboard write happens off-main.
2. **Fix round B (P2):** resumeWorkflowRun + amendWorkflowRunSettings actions on the run
   sheet; deleteQueueItem in the queue strip; find-in-conversation (search bar over rows).
3. **Fix round C (P3):** unsubscribe-on-exit in the conversation teardown; selection
   tooltip/actions + selection side session; suggested prompts on draft; quota banner in the
   conversation (reuse the ADR-020 quota plane); pending-command recovery banner; sessions
   -index subscription for live task activity; interaction snooze.
4. **Fix round D (P4 polish):** attachment preview source; richer assistant artifact
   previews; CUA row grouping; conversation share link modes.

Acceptance for round A: on the rig, `MOCK_HOOKS=1` renders the review card and a
trust_selected round-trip flips item states live (mock handlers exist); answering either
approval class empties the Approvals inbox without leaving the screen.

Verification record: emulator+relay rig ran ~1h with 2 crash-reconnect cycles (emulator
memory-pressure deaths, the known 8GB constraint); no app-side crash, ANR, or error-dialog
was observed at any point.

Unit suites (all 17 modules, `testDebugUnitTest` + `test`): **1487 tests, 0 failures,
0 skipped** at `fd7046a` (fresh XML aggregation across every module's build/test-results).
Three `ConnectionHubWritePathTest` sweeps on this machine hit the documented timing-flake
class — a different test failed each sweep (`draft persists…` then `pending approval…`,
both `TimeoutCancellationException` at the class's 20s/15s `withTimeout` waits), and the
full class passed `--rerun-tasks` and in the final all-module pass; exonerated as machine
timing, not an app defect. The final clean all-module run: BUILD SUCCESSFUL, 368 tasks.

## Part D — pass-2 live emulation

### D1. Newly found defects

- **GAP-A8 (crash, P1): the ENTIRE outbound attachment surface crashes the app — three
  deterministic FATALs, reproduced live on every arm.** Composer `+` → menu offers
  Mention a file / Photo / Attach a file / Take photo. Tapping **Photo**:
  `IllegalArgumentException: Can only use lower 16 bits for requestCode` at
  `androidx.fragment.app.FragmentActivity.checkForValidRequestCode` launched from
  `WriteComponents.kt:832` (`photoPicker.launch(PickVisualMediaRequest)`) — FATAL, process
  dead. Tapping **Attach a file**: identical FATAL (16:14:38, pid 6454) from the same
  registry path (`docPicker.launch`, `WriteComponents.kt:844`). Tapping **Take photo**:
  identical FATAL (16:15:33, pid 6657, `cameraLauncher.launch`, `WriteComponents.kt:854`).
  Only **Mention a file** works (pure text insertion, verified "@" inserted). The three
  launchers are registered at `WriteComponents.kt:657-668` via
  `rememberLauncherForActivityResult`; the request code derived for this registration exceeds
  the 16-bit FragmentActivity limit, so launch() throws before the picker ever opens. Shipped
  in `eb5ae90` (phase-9 attachments) and never exercised on-device (pass 1 verified only the
  inbound attachment render). A primary feature kills the app 3/3 taps — top of the fix order.
- **GAP-A6 (UI break, P2): the task-search overlay draws in the status-bar band and its
  result rows are stacked, overlapped, and dead.** The search field renders at window level
  with zero inset handling — `tasks_search_field` bounds `[44,11][1036,165]`, i.e. under the
  system clock/battery, which render on top of the field. The single result row measured
  `[0,0][1080,117]` (`tasks_search_hit_synth-task-3`, title at `[44,28]`) — behind the clock
  AND under the field. Mechanism: the search field + result rows are emitted as bare siblings
  AFTER the Scaffold at the screen-function top level (`TaskListScreen.kt:390-443`), so every
  sibling lands top-start in the host Box with no `statusBars()` padding. Two taps at the hit
  row produced no navigation and no logs — the only hit is effectively unusable on device.
- **GAP-A7 (contract break, P2): search results do not replace the grouped list.** The code
  comment promises "results REPLACE the grouped list" and `return`s at
  `TaskListScreen.kt:450`, but the Scaffold body (Automations/Workflows/Pinned/Workspace
  sections) is emitted BEFORE that point and always composes; on device the grouped list
  stayed fully visible below the (misplaced) results. The H1.1 contract is broken on-device.
- **WATCH (unconfirmed, needs a dedicated leg): sending slash text while queue mode is armed**
  ("/deploy prod" with the composer in "Keep typing to queue follow-up changes" mode) rode
  the wire (`sendConversationCommandV4` acked ok in 89 ms) but produced no timeline row and
  left the draft in the composer; a second send after toggling queue mode off acked ok
  (660 ms) and cleared the draft. Likely queue-item semantics rather than a defect, but the
  first send's wire-acked/no-row/no-clear combination is worth a scripted rig leg before
  calling it clean.

### D4. Rig learnings for the next pass

1. **The mock's command effects are wired to ONE hardcoded session** (`MockWorkspace.sessionId

   Interaction's `pendingInteractions:[]`, "(answered)" rows, sendText echo) is pushed to

   the pass-2 answer was sent from Synthetic task 2's card, and the "(answered)" row appeared
   in SYNTHETIC task 1's timeline (screenshot 27) while task 2's card never cleared. This is a
   RIG routing artifact, not an app defect — and it re-frames pass 1's GAP-A2 evidence: the
   "pinned card cleared via state patch" observation happened because pass 1 answered inside
   the default session. The inbox-never-clears claim is INDEPENDENT of this (re-confirmed this
   pass on both classes) but future rig legs must run interaction flows in synth-task-1.

   re-dump bounds after every chrome change (three tap misses this round came from stale
   coordinates).

   detached (`nohup … &`); the app reconnects within seconds of the socket returning.

## Part G — pass-3 live emulation

### G1. Newly found defects

- **GAP-A9 (UX break, P2): the queue-mode composer has NO send affordance while the agent is
  stoppable — the exact state queue mode exists for.** The primary composer control MORPHS
  STOP↔SEND on `canStop && stopState==STOPPABLE` alone (`WriteComponents.kt:910-912`); in
  ENQUEUE mode the slot shows STOP unconditionally and SEND simply does not exist. Live proof
  in synth-task-1 (the effect-routing session): sent "ping-rig3" → composer flipped to "Keep
  typing to queue follow-up changes" + Queued chip; typed "/deploy prod" → dump + pixels show
  the composer holding the text with only +/Queued/Stop present (`/tmp/walk3/05`); IME Enter
  inserts a NEWLINE (`/deploy prod&#10;`, no IME send action is configured —
  `composerKeyboardOptions` sets only capitalization/ascii, `WriteComponents.kt:1155-1164`);
  the relay log records NO send call. The Queued pill is a passive label
  (`composer_queue_pill`, `:886-904`) and the QueueStrip renders only when items exist. The
  user is invited to type but cannot dispatch until the agent stops or the control flips
  non-stoppable — and tapping Stop is self-defeating (it kills the run). Desktop contract is
  the INVERSE and is the fix anchor: `showStopControl = canStop && !hasDraftToSubmit`
  (`ConversationComposer.tsx:1136`, with the header comment "running+空草稿 → Stop") — a
  typed draft ALWAYS keeps the send path, even mid-run; the desktop additionally supports
  modified-Enter delivery reversal (`:1099`). Fix: gate the morph on a blank draft (desktop
  semantics), optionally add an IME send action; pin with a Robolectric test that the send
  control exists with a non-blank draft while `canStop`.
- **GAP-A10 (UX, P4): a rejected direct-endpoint add closes the dialog and discards every
  typed field; the only feedback is a transient auto-dismiss toast.** Mechanism:
  `AddDirectEndpointDialog`'s onAdd sets `showAddDialog = false` BEFORE the outcome is known
  (`SettingsScreen.kt:397`), and `ConnectionHub.addDirectEndpoint` probes the server with a
  10s budget before saving (`ConnectionHub.kt:1190`) — so the dialog is already gone while
  the probe runs and a Rejected outcome can only surface as the `switchMessage` toast
  (`AutoDismissMessage`). Live: added "Probe" → `ws://10.0.2.2:18999/ws` (dead port) → at +3s
  the dialog is closed, no endpoint card, no visible error. Secondary: the fallback-URL
  candidates are never validated client-side (the `valid` gate checks only the primary URL's
  scheme, `SettingsScreen.kt:439`; candidates pass through a bare split/trim/filter) while
  the dialog note claims "Validated before saving". Fix: keep the dialog open on Rejected
  with an inline error, validate candidate schemes with the same gate.

### P4. Rig learnings for the next pass

1. **The rendered-screenshot scale is NON-UNIFORM vs device pixels in this environment**
   (x-scale ≈1.19 and y-scale ≈1.17 observed on the SAME capture, and it drifts between
   captures). Deriving tap coords from a global scale misses. Correct method: take the
   dump, tap ONLY nodes the dump bounds directly, and for AX-merged/[0,0] rows derive x
   from a same-row dump-anchored sibling and y from the adjacent-row pitch — never from
   the displayed image.
2. **The context-sheet "Model calls"/"Share" chip line sits directly under the sheet's
   DRAG HANDLE touch target** — a tap landing a few px high long-presses the handle
   (a "Drag handle" toast renders) and can close the just-opened pane. Approach the chip
   row from its own dump-pitch coordinates, and prefer the Files/Git/Terminal row (fully
   AX-exposed at y≈2041) as the anchor: the second chip line is one ~84px pitch below.
3. **`input text` inserts at cursor position 0 when a field gains focus without a caret
   position** ("@s" typed as "s@") — `keyevent KEYCODE_MOVE_END` first, or type the full
   query in one `input text` after clearing.
4. **The mock's group store MUTATES for `createTaskGroup` + group assignment** (the new
   group renders and the assigned task moves under it), unlike rename/archive where the
   ack doesn't mutate the task store. Group-plane legs are therefore fully observable
   end-to-end; rename/archive assertions must target the wire receipt, not the label.
5. Stale-dump + dialog learning reconfirmed twice more (post-Archive-sheet dump kept
   pre-cancel content; post-Rename dump kept the dialog). Screenshot after every dialog
   transition; fresh dump only after a route change.
6. `input tap` on the confirm sheet while the keyboard is up hits DISPLACED buttons —
   dismiss the keyboard (`keyevent 111`) before tapping dialog confirms (cost one
   no-op Rename round).

  fell back to `No snapshots in this session`. Consequence: the Restore affordance (which
  needs an EARLIER checkpoint in the list, `GitScreen.kt:817-823`) is unreachable after any
  app restart, so the phone can only restore inside one uninterrupted screen mount while

   shade deep-link leg is cheap and repeatable with no new mock arm. The connection-lost
   kill-leg from pass 7 remains the other standing notification leg.

   of the approvals screen — back from that conversation lands in the INBOX, not Tasks;
   from there one more back reaches Tasks. Plan back-presses to the route stack, not to

Shipped receipts: **267 `WebRemoteControl` + 108 `web-remote-control` hits** in the audited

that exists in a browser tab), but "on par" must now answer the browser-shell question:
either document the plane under B3 or plan interop. Leaving it unowned leaves a whole
product plane unrecorded.

  taskId != null` (`NotificationBroker.kt:138-141`) and passes them into the Spec. But the
  §15-S13 background re-post — `onBackgroundEntry` (`NotificationBroker.kt:179-188`) —
  builds its Spec WITHOUT the `actions` parameter, so every unseen attention record that
  surfaces on background entry loses its buttons. And the fresh path is foreclosed in the
  PRIMARY companion flow: an approval arriving while the app is foregrounded is
  §9.9-suppressed at post time (recorded unseen, nothing posted), and its ONLY subsequent

  :: key=interaction:q-rig-1` and `…mock-approva… (background entry)` (13:19:27) — and the

  but NO action PendingIntents, with the per-package ranking counter reading

  rig). Net: `NotificationActionReceiver` + the post-decision haptic (C3) are fully wired
  but starved — the buttons exist only in the rare race of a fresh approval arriving while
  the app is ALREADY backgrounded. Remedy: replicate the permission-gated `actions` list in
  `onBackgroundEntry`'s Spec (the record already holds kind/interactionId/taskId — the
  same SpecAction builder applies).

### AE2. NEW defect

- **GAP-A13 (UX break, P2): the goal-verb refusal feedback is invisible at refusal time —
  and when it finally paints, it is stale.** Three wire-confirmed `pauseGoal` rejections
  produced NO SendNotice bar in five captures across six minutes (the IME-up posture a
  real user sends from). The bar only painted after a keyboard-down layout pass minutes
  later — showing the PAUSE copy ("Goal pause was refused (the goal may not be pausable
  right now).") at [0,0] AX bounds while the most recent dispatch had been a (tap-missed)
  resume attempt. Static mechanism: `_sendNotice` is a `MutableStateFlow` READ (`.value`)
  inside the five-source combine that builds `ConversationUiState`
  (`ConversationViewModel.kt:166` vs the read at `:212`) — a notice-only change cannot
  re-emit the state, so the composer renders no banner until some UNRELATED source (draft,
  session patches, pending-sends, rows) happens to emit. This is the exact FIELD-class bug
  the vc21 draft fix documented and repaired for the draft (the WriteState
  draft-as-combine-source comment at `:162-170`); the notice never got the same treatment.
  Remedy: make `_sendNotice` a combine source (fold into WriteState) or collect it into
  the uiState directly. The user-facing failure today: a refused slash verb looks like a
  dead button — draft stays, no signal — for an unbounded time.

### AF1. NEW GAP-G41 (P3): multi-workspace management — add/open/switch/reorder/remote

The desktop treats workspaces as FIRST-CLASS MANAGED OBJECTS: `WorkspaceSidebar.tsx`
renders a "Projects" section (`workspaceSidebar.projectsSection`) with per-workspace
tabs (task groups keyed by `buildTaskWorkspaceKey(path, identity)`, loading state per
group, `workspace.context.lastActivity` "Last active {time}"), an add-project "+" menu
(`workspaceSidebar.addProject` → "Open folder" (`workspace.openFolder`) + "Remote
connection" (`remote.trigger`, Cloud icon)), and a full DRAG-REORDER plane
(`DndContext` + `verticalListSortingStrategy`, `handleWorkspaceDragStart/End` —
user-orderable, persisted). The remote path is a four-step wizard (`remote.wizard`:
Choose method → Connection settings → Connecting → Choose remote directory) with
saved-connection history (`remote.history.empty` "No matching saved connections"),
WSL-UNC prompting (`workspace.wslUncPrompt`), and an SSH/WSL/Docker remote-environment
model (the Computer-Use catalog copy names all three). Supporting strings:
"Add new workspace", "Start from scratch", `workspace.backToWorkspace`,
`workspaceSidebar.noProjects` "No open projects". Asar receipts (shipped): "Add
project" ×1, "No open projects" ×1, "Remote connection" ×4, "Add new workspace" ×1,
"Start from scratch" ×1, `workspaceSidebar.projectsSection` ×3,
`workspaceSidebar.addProject` ×3, `remote.trigger` ×4, "Choose remote directory" ×1,
`workspace.context.lastActivity` ×3, `remote.history.empty` ×3, "Open folder" ×2,
`workspace.openFolder` ×4. THE PHONE: workspaces exist only as a PASSIVE grouping —
tasks arrive grouped by `workspaceIdentityKey` and render under collapsible workspace
headers (`TaskListScreen`/`WorkspaceCollapse.kt`); there is no add, no open-folder, no
active-workspace switch, no reorder, and no remote-environment concept anywhere in the
app (grep: zero consumers of any of the above strings' intents). Scope note: pass 6's
Q3 recorded the SSH DIALOG as a desktop-form BOUNDARY — that disposition stands for the
dialog itself; G41 is the broader capability gap (the workspace MODEL the dialog feeds:
multi-workspace registration/switching/ordering), which no pass had enumerated. The
companion-shaped remedy is a workspace switcher/manager over the workspaces the phone
already RECEIVES, not a folder picker.

## Binding rules for every fix session

1. **Repo + branch.** Work in this repo on `fix/vc51` cut from `main`; land per the
   release policy (ADDITIVE = signed draft / BREAKING = draft PR; a human promotes; never
   push unless Ernest says). Every hand-built APK carries the
   `zcode-android-release-meta` block (ReleaseParser fails closed).
2. **One finding ≥ one commit**, message form `fix(<ID>): <mechanism>`. One commit may
   close several rows ONLY when they are one shared mechanism (rule 11) — say so in the
   message and tick every covered row.
3. **Re-read before fixing.** Re-read the finding's entry above (its Part citations) and
   its roadmap row before writing code; honor the pass-12 re-scopes (G32/G37/E4) and the
   AI2-narrowed A11 scope (the nav-inset and row-overlap halves are REFUTED — no work
   there).
4. **TEST-FIRST with shape fidelity.** The pin that reproduces the recorded defect shape
   is written and RED at the pre-fix commit before the fix lands: A8 = a three-arm
   `launch()`-without-throwing test; A2 = inbox-clears-on-answer for BOTH classes
   (state-plane + row-anchored); A13 = uiState re-emits on a notice-only change; A12 = a
   background-entry re-post carries two action PendingIntents; A11 = a landscape
   composition pin on the pinned card's visible height.
5. **Every fix ships its pin in the same commit.** No fix row is ticked on pins alone and
   no pin lands without its fix. Mock/rig changes are separate `tools/mockzcode` commits
   with self-tests green (`:tools:mockzcode:jar` + `:tools:mockzcode:test`).
6. **COMMIT BEFORE ANY RIG LEG.** No uncommitted work may exist when an emulator, mock
   relay, or gradle suite runs (recorded hazards: emulator beside gradle pools = timing
   flakes; free snapshots/intermediates before cold boots; kill the mock ONLY via
   `pkill -f MockRelayMainKt`, never by port).
7. **Fresh full-suite baseline + zero-new-names gate.** At each phase start, record the
   full-suite baseline at the pre-phase commit — 17 modules means `testDebugUnitTest` for
   the Android modules AND `test` for the six JVM modules (the 2026-10-21 blind-spot
   lesson). After each fix commit, re-run the touched modules and name-diff every new
   failing test against the baseline; ALSO assert the gradle task-failure list holds only
   test-failure tasks and no module stopped emitting test XML (test-compile failures are
   invisible to a name-diff). Every new name is chased or exonerated in writing.
8. **~150-line/stop rule.** Any single change beyond ~150 lines or spanning >3 modules
   stops for a checkpoint commit + suite re-run. GAP-A1's card is the expected exception —
   split it into wire→VM→UI sub-commits under one row.
9. **Independent per-phase verification.** A phase is done only when its exit gate passes
   on a FRESH emulator+relay rig leg (cold boot, the standing all-flags arming + the
   phase's named mock arms), with receipts appended to this report and the rows ticked.
10. **Record duty.** Tick rows here as their Accept criteria pass; add reusable learnings
    to AGENTS.md; keep the one-report-file append-only discipline; record mock-side
    behaviors that are rig fidelity (not app truth) so later passes don't chase them.
11. **Shared-remedy preference.** Cluster findings that share a mechanism into one remedy
    when it does not blur ownership: A6+A7 (one overlay rewrite), A8 (one registry helper,
    three arms), A12 (one Spec-action builder shared with the fresh path), G7+G8
    (selection family), G16+G17+G28+G40 (preview/search-scope family), G25/G27/G30
    (INV-9 viewer pattern), G22/G23/G24 (settings-plane family), and the
    modeled-never-sent sweep (G3/G4/G6/G8 — per AH3 the zero-send-site family is
    createSelectionSideSession, deleteQueueItem, snoozeInteractionAutoResolution,
    cancelWorkflowRun, resumeWorkflowRun, amendWorkflowRunSettings, renameSession,
    deleteSession).

Sixteen P3 rows in four clusters: protocol hygiene, conversation affordances,
plan/quota/usage, and presentation/workspace management (with the two boundary decisions
that must produce dated answers).

  (wasted frames, stale-stream risk after reconnects). Fix: send unsubscribe-on-exit in

## Dated boundary decisions (G40 + G35)

- **G40 (workspace search scope / .zcodeignore rules editor) — B3 boundary, dated 2026-10-31:**
  the .zcodeignore rules editor (WorkspaceFileSearchSection.tsx, "Sync from .gitignore",
  "Restore default rules") is DESKTOP-SIDE authoring — it configures the desktop's own
  workspace-file-search indexing, a capability whose infrastructure (the local index, the
  sync pipeline) the phone does not host. The phone's bounded file plane stays as shipped:
  the read-only Files browser, the git read channel, and (NEW this phase, G9/RIG-2) the
  composer @-mention workspace-file search honoring the desktop's indexed results — the
  search itself runs desktop-side where the rules live. Editor/UI for the RULES is a
  desktop-authoring surface under the B3 precedent (hooks configuration, workflow
  authoring). Revisit only if a pass shows the mention panel's results ignoring rules
  users set (it cannot — the host filters).
- **G35 (the shipped web-remote-control browser companion) — B3/interop decision, dated
  2026-10-31:** the phone remains the NATIVE client and the browser shell is recorded as a
  PARALLEL surface, not a parity target: push notifications with shade actions, the
  glance widget, offline cache, launcher shortcuts, sealed multi-endpoint credentials, and
  voice input are phone-only (B4) and cannot exist in a browser tab. No interop work is
  planned: the surfaces share the host's v4 plane but nothing else, and bridging them
  (e.g. handing a browser session to the phone) has no user story. **The Relay V2 WATCH
  (JWT bearer, device roles, 60 s WS tokens — NOT in the shipped 3.14.5 asar) is carried
  verbatim into any future pairing/transport work**: a desktop update that flips the relay
  to V2 would strand the phone's pairing path, and any such change re-runs the W2 drift
  greps BEFORE the phone ships a release against it.

## A2 (FIXED — a real defect). G32's "GitWriteWireTest create/switch round-trip" did not exist, and the mock was losing the branch on the wire

The G32 receipt cited "`GitWriteWireTest` (the create/switch round-trip over the real
transport)"; at completion the class held only stage/unstage/discard, commit/push/
branches decode, and the switch **refusal** decode — no create/switch success round-trip
existed over the wire (that path was covered only mock-internally + the live rig leg).
Writing the cited pin **RED'd a real defect** (`484a64b6`): `MockZCode.str()` returns
`""` (never null) for a missing key, so the `switchBranch`/`createBranchAndSwitch`
handler's `str("targetBranchName") ?: str("branchName")` elvis never fell through — the
transport's `gitCreateBranchAndSwitch` sends the wire key `branchName`, the mock read
`""`, and **every create ack silently lost the branch**: the response carried
`branchName:""` (decoding to null) and the served summary/branch-list head never moved —
the exact "the static summary doesn't mutate post-create" class the Phase-4 exit-gate
recorded and RIG-5 was believed to have retired for the create verb (RIG-5's mutation
fix was real but its self-test fed the git-channel-promise spelling `targetBranchName`,
which worked; only the transport-wire spelling was broken). Fix: the handler reads via
`strOrNull` so BOTH spellings win; the new wire pin (create → the served head follows the
ack → switch back to main → the head follows) is GREEN, and
`MockZCodeRig5FidelitySelfTest` stays green (the promise path is unchanged).

## A3 (record + one new pin). RIG-5's "10 pins" — corrected to the real list, plus the one genuinely-missing face

The roadmap row's "10 pins (routing ×3, store mutations ×2, git mutation ×1, regression
controls ×2, default-routing preservation ×2)" does not match the class's test list (7
@Test at `6bd095ed` — routing ×2, default-preservation ×1, store ×2, git ×1, control ×1);
it was a loose assertion-count, and the Phase-5 gate's own name-diff correctly used 7.
One routing face the RIG-5 commit itself claims (the row-command effects:
retry/fork/rewind/**feedback**) had no pin; it now does (assistant-feedback journals on
the CALLING session and the feedback lands on the echoed row, `484a64b6`). The class is
**8 @Test**: routing ×3 (sendText, interaction push, feedback) + default-preservation ×1
+ store mutations ×2 + git mutation ×1 + regression control ×1.

  the main `Column(Modifier.fillMaxSize()…)` (`TaskListScreen.kt:249`, sections at `:403`, tasks
  box at `:419-424`) which has NO `verticalScroll`, so the tasks Box receives ~zero remaining
  height: zero task rows compose (uiautomator max text y=2067, NO scrollable container in the
  hierarchy), every swipe/fling is a no-op, and the search FAB is pushed below the fold too.

  "Tasks no-scroll landscape" small is the same class; Phase 4's section additions made it
  PORTRAIT-fatal. Real desktops serve automations, so every real user with ≥1 automation loses
  their task list. Remedy: make the main body scrollable or move the sections into the tasks
  LazyColumn as items.
- **GAP-A15 (misleading copy, P3): a SUCCESSFUL hook trust renders the OFFLINE banner.**
  `ConversationViewModel.trustHooks` on ACCEPTED emits `"Trusted N hook(s) — the session
  continues."` keyed `SendNotice.Key.ROW_ACTION_OFFLINE` ("honest generic info key" comment,
  `ConversationViewModel.kt:788`) — but the renderer maps that key to the fixed string
  `notice_row_action_offline` = "Offline — the action was not sent. Nothing changed."
  (`WriteComponents.kt:1290`), ignoring the custom message. Live proof: the trust succeeded
  (`grantWorkspaceHookTrust ok in 47ms`) and the strip read "Offline — the action was not sent.
  Nothing changed." Remedy: a dedicated `HOOK_TRUST_APPLIED` key + string.
- **GAP-A16 (UX small, P3): the composer squeezes out of view when a tall pinned interaction card
  + queue strip are present and the IME opens.** Reproduced twice (screenshots 47 and 65): with
  the approval card + "Queued (2)" strip pinned, opening the keyboard fills the viewport with
  card+strip and the composer (draft + buttons) renders BEHIND the IME — typing works blind.
  The GAP-A4 family (sheet-level imePadding) is fixed; this is the conversation-composer sibling
  under the tall-pinned-stack condition.

## Part AM — pass-14 live emulation

### AM1. NEW rig blocker found and solved (recorded because it will bite every future pass)

**The cold boot left the emulator DUAL-HOMED on the same subnet** — `eth0 10.0.2.15/24` AND
`wlan0 10.0.2.16/24`, both with a `10.0.2.0/24` route. The result was a route flap: TCP to
`10.0.2.2:18100` alternated between working (`nc` exit 0) and `Network is unreachable`, the app's
relay connect timed out at 10 s, the bootstrap retried 3× and degraded — **with ZERO frames ever
reaching the relay** (`relay.log` held nothing but the READY banner). Two app restarts and a relay
restart changed nothing. Fix: `adb shell svc wifi disable` (single-home eth0), after which the
handshake and AUTH succeeded immediately and the whole walk proceeded with no further network
faults. Diagnostic signature to recognize it: relay log EMPTY + `hub.connectFailed :: TIMEOUT
connect timed out after 10000ms` + `adb shell nc` toggling between success and "Network is
unreachable". (Not an app defect: the app retried and degraded exactly as designed.)

Second rig trap, self-inflicted: a manual WebSocket probe from the HOST to the mock relay wedges
the relay's single-listener session slot — after it, the app's `auth_ack` timed out for every
connection until the relay was restarted (`pkill -f MockRelayMainKt`). Never hand-shake the mock
outside the app; use `nc` (no upgrade) to prove reachability.

### AM3. Reconnect leg — the G43 re-adjudication receipt

Relay killed mid-pass (`pkill -f MockRelayMainKt`, never lsof-by-port) and restarted:

- App: `relay.lost` → RECONNECTING → (relay up) → `hub.phase → CONNECTED`
- **`relay.recovered :: subscriptions=2 snapshotReplace=true`** — both hub-lifetime topics
  re-anchored, and the ack reported a SNAPSHOT REPLACEMENT (atomic projection swap, §15.5)
- Wire order on the new connection (`relay2.log` ids 5–6, app log 20:37:06.829–.849):
  **`subscribeSessionsIndexV4 ok in 8ms`** then **`subscribeWorkspaceConfigV4 ok in 10ms`**
- `hub.bootstrapReplayed :: in-connect payload applied (no re-fetch)`

This matters for the ledger: Part AK1 listed `resyncSessionsIndexV4` / `resyncWorkspaceConfigV4`
as desktop-only and attributed the phone's index freshness to "the next pushed patch". The phone
actually re-SUBSCRIBES both topics on every reconnect and treats the ack as a snapshot
replacement — which is the same freshness guarantee the desktop's resync route provides (the
desktop's `resyncV4Route` helper carries `topic + subscriptionId + optional base` to delta-replay an
owned subscription; the phone's re-subscribe carries `base` by absence and gets a full snapshot).
Both are gap-free; the mechanisms differ. G43 therefore narrows from "the phone never resyncs" to
"the phone uses re-subscribe+snapshot instead of an owned-subscription resync" — a hygiene
difference with no observable staleness. Re-adjudication recorded in Part AO.

### AM4. NEW defect found this pass (mock, not app)

**The mock's `resolveInteraction` cleared BOTH pending slots regardless of which interaction was
answered.** Live chain: DB ground truth (`interactions` table) shows `mock-approval-push-1`
answered at 20:04:45 and `q-rig-1` (the scripted AskUserQuestion) flipping to RESOLVED **83 ms
earlier in the same second with no wire command naming it** — because the handler did
`script.pendingPermission = null; script.pendingUserInput = null` unconditionally. c2bcdc1b fixed
the HOOK half of this class (the patch no longer emits an empty list); the sibling-interaction half
was still live. The app behaved correctly throughout (the state list is the whole truth → an
absent interaction resolves by-elsewhere, which is the documented §20.3 rule).

Fixed this round test-first (see the round record below): one shared `pendingInteractionList()`
builder feeds the snapshot AND every patch, the handler clears only the slot the answered id names,
and the same class in `resolveInteractionElsewhere()` (both slots + `pendingInteractions: []`) was
closed with it.

## Part AN — pass-14 macOS enumeration (REA, new angle: the dynamic-channel adapter surface)

Asar digest re-measured byte-identical (`99e280fb90b626cc…`); fresh full analysis retained as
`ev_05d09d8f…` (supersedes the pass-13 cite). New enumeration angle this pass: instead of counting
wire METHODS (pass 1/13), count the host adapter's DYNAMIC CHANNEL registrations and classify each
against the phone's channel inventory.

### AN1. Desktop dynamic channels: 28 registered, 4 phone counterparts, the rest classified

The shipped host registers 28 `onDynamic*` channel handlers (`onDynamicControllerFrame`,
`onDynamicConversationFrame`, `onDynamicConversationTelemetryFact`, `onDynamicCuaPermissionObservation`,
`onDynamicData`, `onDynamicChange`, `onDynamicExit`, `onDynamicImportProgress`,
`onDynamicLocalTtftFacts`, `onDynamicMcpResourceSamples`, `onDynamicMcpTelemetry`,
`onDynamicPluginOperationProgress`, `onDynamicProcessResourceSample`,
`onDynamicProviderRuntimeHeadersRequest`, `onDynamicPublishProgress`, `onDynamicSessionEvent`,
`onDynamicSessionRuntimePreferencesRequest`, `onDynamicSessionsIndexFrame`,
`onDynamicStorageStartupState`, `onDynamicStreamEvent`, `onDynamicTaskEvent`, `onDynamicTaskReady`,
`onDynamicTaskTerminalOutcome`, `onDynamicToolExecResource`, `onDynamicWorkspaceConfigFrame`,
`onDynamicWorkspaceEvent`, `onDynamicWorkspaceProviderRuntimeHeadersCancelled`,
`onDynamicWorkspaceProviderRuntimeHeadersRequest`).

The phone listens on four channel pairs: `zcode-agent.onDynamicConversationFrame` (which also
topic-routes workspace-config frames — `ConversationGateway` branches on the
`workspace-config/` prefix), `zcode-agent.onDynamicSessionsIndexFrame`, `terminal.onDynamicData`,
`terminal.onDynamicExit`. The controller trio is confirmed by its own neighbourhood — the
`onDynamicControllerFrame` handler sits beside `subscribeControllerV4` / `resyncControllerV4` /
`unsubscribeControllerV4` (the shipped host's controller plane), which is exactly what makes G42 a
plane-level (not frame-level) gap.

| Desktop channel(s) | Classification |
| --- | --- |
| `onDynamicConversationFrame`, `onDynamicSessionsIndexFrame`, `onDynamicWorkspaceConfigFrame`, `onDynamicData`/`onDynamicExit` | **Implemented** (4 phone listens; the config plane rides the conversation channel by topic) |
| `onDynamicControllerFrame` | **G42** (unchanged): the host WindowHostController task-list plane — richer successor to the phone's bootstrap + sessions-index + per-screen commands. No user-facing breakage |
| `onDynamicProcessResourceSample`, `onDynamicMcpResourceSamples`, `onDynamicMcpTelemetry`, `onDynamicToolExecResource` | **Desktop-only observability**: renderer-side resource/telemetry acquisition for the desktop's own dashboards. The phone has its own usage surface (`usage-stats.getEntitlementSnapshot` + the Usage screen) and no continuous-sampling requirement |
| `onDynamicLocalTtftFacts`, `onDynamicConversationTelemetryFact` | **Desktop-only telemetry**: first-token-latency facts for the desktop's perf overlays. Not a companion surface |
| `onDynamicChange` | **Desktop-only**: the file-WATCHER change emitter (workspace file watching). The phone has no file watcher by design (Files panel is a read-only query plane) |
| `onDynamicStorageStartupState` | **Desktop-only**: the host's storage boot gate. The phone's equivalent is connection/bootstrap state |
| `onDynamicImportProgress`, `onDynamicPublishProgress`, `onDynamicPluginOperationProgress` | **Desktop-only**: conversation import + share publish + plugin operation progress — desktop-heavy workflows whose phone analogues are read-only viewers (Plugins/Skills) |
| `onDynamicCuaPermissionObservation` | **G44** (unchanged, boundary): CUA permission observation belongs to the desktop's permission recorder; the phone renders CUA tool rows (verified G18) |
| `onDynamicTaskEvent`, `onDynamicTaskReady`, `onDynamicTaskTerminalOutcome`, `onDynamicStreamEvent` | **Mapped, different mechanism**: the desktop's TASK-lifecycle surface (task events / ready / terminal outcome / stream). The phone covers the same states on two planes it already owns — `onDynamicConversationFrame` (run lifecycle rows + `control.phase`/`sessionEnded`) and `onDynamicSessionsIndexFrame` (per-task live activity: Live / Needs you / Ended, rendered by `TaskListScreen`'s sessions-index activity). Nothing the desktop reports here is invisible on the phone |
| `onDynamicSessionEvent`, `onDynamicWorkspaceEvent` | **Transport-internal**: the host's session/workspace multiplexer buses (they feed the frames above). Not separately client-facing |
| `onDynamicProviderRuntimeHeadersRequest` / `…Cancelled` / `onDynamicSessionRuntimePreferencesRequest` | **Desktop-only**: host↔provider runtime header injection and per-session runtime prefs — model-credential plumbing that lives on the desktop by design (the phone never holds provider credentials) |

**Verdict:** zero new phone-side gaps from this angle. Every unpaired desktop channel is either
desktop-only telemetry/ops plumbing, transport-internal, or an already-classified boundary
(G42/G44). The phone's four listens are exactly the client-facing set the companion needs.

### AN2. Two more desktop planes confirmed AT PARITY this pass

1. **Slash commands.** The host's projection carries `slashCommands: w.slashCommands ?? PU` where
   `PU = []` — i.e. the desktop has NO static builtin slash catalog; commands come from session
   state. The phone already parses and renders the wire catalog (`V4WorkspaceConfig.slashCommands`
   + `SlashCommandParser.kt` "parseV4VisibleSlashCommand" port + the three-section panel). Parity
   confirmed structurally; the live refusal leg (`/goal pause`) re-verified the command plane.
2. **Config options.** Desktop projection: `configOptions: fa(w.settings)`; the phone decodes
   `configOptions[]` from the workspace-config snapshot, renders the mode/effort/model chips, and
   drives `setThoughtLevel` with echo reconciliation. Parity confirmed on both planes.

### AN3. Automation / off-peak tool-denylist constants (new, recorded for completeness)

The host defines `JP = ["CronCreate","CronUpdate","CronDelete"]` (automation runs) and
`YP = ["OffPeakCreate"]` (idle-time runs), merged into each run's `toolDenylist`. The phone does not
run prompts for those planes (it starts/pauses/edits automations and idle-time tasks via commands),
so no phone-side counterpart is required — recorded so a future pass does not re-derive it as a gap.

## Part AP2 — mock defect found live, fixed test-first (commit `0f88f64b`)

`respondWorkspaceHookReview` wrote `script.hookReviewsResolved` but NOTHING read the flag:
`scriptedHookInteraction()` sat in `pendingInteractionList()` unconditionally, so the next full
state emission re-asserted the RESPONDED review as pending. Live case: trust-confirm →
`grantWorkspaceHookTrust ok` → "Trusted 2 hook(s)" → the follow-up command's patch carried the hook
interaction again → the trust card CAME BACK and re-froze the timeline. Third member of the
resolve-class family (c2bcdc1b pass 13, 2d7e61d5 pass 14). The app is contract-correct (key-level
replacement trusts `pendingInteractions` as the whole truth). Pass 14's A15 leg masked it because it
ended at the applied notice without a follow-up command.

Fix + pin: `scriptedHookInteraction()` gates on the flag; `MockZCodeHookMergeSelfTest` gains
"a RESPONDED hook review stays resolved in every later snapshot and patch" — RED on the unfixed
tree (1 of 5 failed, AssertionError at the snapshot assertion, the exact live resurrect), GREEN
after the one-line gate; `:tools:mockzcode:test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL (65 tests). **Live re-verification
on a clean rig (fresh `pm clear` + re-pair + fresh interaction ids): trust → confirm → follow-up
Send-now commands → the hook card STAYS RESOLVED** (was the resurrect trigger pre-fix).

## Part AP3 — the "inert interaction cards" rig saga, resolved: rig fidelity + correct app guard

Across relay generations 2–3, taps on pinned interaction-card buttons appeared dead: the card
persisted, answered cards re-answered to the honest "Already handled on the desktop." degrade, and
no wire command left the app. Root cause (verified by the flushed relay ledger — **grep the relay
log only after a flush; its stdout is block-buffered and stale greps mislead**):

1. **The mock's scripted interaction ids are constants** (`mock-approval-1`, `q-rig-1`,
   `hook-rig`) reused by EVERY relay generation, while the app's interaction lifecycle persists in
   Room. After relay-1 answered those ids, every later generation's same-id cards were correctly
   refused by the app's INV-4 duplicate guard (`DuplicateNoOp` — "a LIVE pending entry is never
   duplicated") with the honest degrade banner and no wire send. Proof by differential: the pass-15
   push used a UNIQUE id (`mock-approval-push-15`) and its inbox answer worked immediately
   (card resolved, effect ran). The app never misbehaved; **rig remedy for future passes: derive
   scripted interaction ids from a per-relay-generation nonce** (or `pm clear` between relay
   generations, as this pass's closing leg did).
2. A second attribution trap: the push REPLACES the mock's single `pendingPermission` slot, so an
   answer naming the pre-push id matches nothing in `applyCommandEffect` (`hadPermission=false`) —
   combined with (1) this made cards look permanently stuck. Mock fidelity debt, recorded.

Net app-side verdict: the INV-4 guard, the by-elsewhere rule, and the degrade banners all behaved
exactly per contract throughout. No app change.

## Part AQ2 — the hook-trust post-fix semantics, RESOLVED (and a pass-14 receipt explained)

Pass-14's A15 receipt said post-trust "Warm build cache shows Disable + **Revoke** (trusted)", but
this pass post-trust Warm showed Disable WITHOUT Revoke — same APK bytes, so something differed.
Resolution, verified live + in code + in mock history:

1. The app's `HookTrustReviewCard` renders per-item verbs purely from the served payload: Disable
   when `editable`, Revoke when `trustState == "trusted_persistent"`. The ViewModel does NOT apply
   an optimistic local trust update after `respondWorkspaceHookReview` — by contract, the wire is
   the whole truth.
2. The mock's `respondWorkspaceHookReview` (unchanged since 2d7e61d5) updates its internal
   `hookTrustStates` but pushes a **revision-only patch** — no hookReview payload, no
   pendingInteractions re-assert. The app therefore never learns the new per-item states: Warm
   stays as-first-served (Disable, no Revoke). **Mock fidelity debt**: the desktop would publish
   the updated review state; the mock doesn't.
3. So why did pass-14 see Revoke on Warm? Because pre-`0f88f64b` the hook interaction was
   RESURRECTED into every later snapshot/patch — and `scriptedHookInteraction()` re-serves the
   review with the UPDATED `hookTrustStates` applied. Pass-14's "correct per-item verbs" were
   observed **through the resurrection bug's data path**. The post-fix correct path (this pass)
   leaves per-item states as-first-served until a fresh authority re-serves the review.
4. The card itself persisted post-trust (trust mode, checkboxes, Trust button) because the only
   patches that followed were key-absent (revision-only / queue patches) — correct by key-level
   replacement. The decisive NEW receipt: leaving and re-entering the conversation took a fresh
   subscribe + snapshot whose `pendingInteractions` was `[]` (all three resolved/gated) — **the
   app resolved the hook card from the snapshot** (gone from the pinned plane). Key-level
   replacement verified on the SNAPSHOT path, not just patches. (An intermediate stale
   accessibility-tree read during a long-press navigation briefly suggested otherwise — rig
   artifact, superseded by the clean tap-entry receipt.)

## Part AR2 — pass-17 defects (2 P3 + 3 P4, all receipted on device)

**D1 (P3, new): relay-restart recovery race wedges the hub phase machine in DEGRADED with a
healthy wire.** Sequence (fully logged): relay killed + restarted; app reconnected (relay-1
auth matched 18:00:57 → CONNECTED 18:00:58 → bootstrapReplayed); ~3 s later the app's own
recovery loop opened a SECOND connection (relay-2 auth challenge 18:01:01) and the phase machine
flipped to DEGRADED — then never left it: relay-2's auth MATCHED at 18:01:01.524 but no CONNECTED
transition, no bootstrap, and the UI stuck at "Disconnected / Connection lost — reconnecting…"
for ~2.5 minutes while heartbeats + `pair_status_ack` flowed on relay-2 every 10 s (verified
18:01:11→18:02:41). The designed escape hatch works: hub Retry → RECOVERING → CONNECTED →
bootstrapApplied+Replayed (18:03:16). Field trigger: any desktop/relay restart while the phone
holds a live connection (the recovery retry races the first reconnect). Mechanism neighborhood:
the connect()-takeover path (vc47) cancels the predecessor's continuations — the relay-2 takeover
appears to cancel its own phase-completion continuation, leaving the machine in DEGRADED; the
DEGRADED entry itself is the takeover being classified as instability. Casualty: the gen-2 25 s
interaction push fired during the wedge and was lost (no subscribed session). Fix direction: the
takeover path must drive the phase to CONNECTED on auth-match of the SUCCESSOR connection (or the
heartbeat-ack loop must re-armed the phase out of DEGRADED); pin with a two-connection fixture.

**D2 (P3, new): the Context sheet's wrapped second chip row is inert.** At 395 dp with the sheet
fully expanded the chip row wraps to two lines: Files/Git/Terminal (line 1) work; Model calls and
Share (line 2) render visually but their text nodes report `bounds=[0,0][0,0]` in the a11y tree
across three independent dumps and taps at the pixel-true positions produce no navigation and no
`nav.*` log. Blocks the Model-calls viewer and Share on narrow screens. Files/Git/Terminal were
each driven live this pass (receipts above), so the defect is specific to the wrapped row.
Fix direction: the chip-row FlowRow's second-line measurables aren't attached to the semantics
tree — pin with a compose-ui test at 395 dp asserting both rows' chips are clickable and
`onOpenModelCalls`/`onShare` fire.

**D3 (P4, new): `reconcileFromSessionState` re-stamps `resolvedAtMs` on already-resolved
machines.** DB ground truth (run-as sqlite3, interactions table): the gen-1 approval answered
from the conversation card at 17:23:58 (`ackAccepted` → `resolveRecord` → `markResolved`) shows
`resolvedAtMs = 17:41:51` — the disappearance-sweep's unconditional
`resolveRecord(iid, resolvedBySelf=false)` overwrites the truthful self-answer timestamp with the
sweep clock every time a later session-state reconcile runs (the machine is already RESOLVED but
`machine.on(ResolvedElsewhere)` + the `machine.state == RESOLVED` check still route into
resolveRecord). Initial hypothesis "inbox keeps stale actionable rows" REFUTED by the same DB
read (the inbox cleared at answer time; the pending row the inbox showed was the genuinely
unanswered bootstrap approval, whose inbox answer DID stamp synchronously at tap time). Impact:
audit-history only — no UX path reads the overwritten value. Fix direction: skip resolveRecord
when `requests[iid]?.resolvedAtMs != null` (one-line guard + pin).

**D4 (P4, new): the pinned hook-review card's Trust action needs a SHORT swipe to reach.** With
3 hooks + all strips armed the card clips at mid-screen (Watcher row truncated, Trust below the
fold); large vertical swipes scroll the frozen timeline behind the card and do nothing, while a
short swipe INSIDE the card scrolls it and reveals "Trust 2 selected hook(s)". Discoverability
only — the action IS reachable (this pass completed the full trust round-trip). Same composition
family as the pass-2 question-card Submit fix (that fix made the card content scrollable; the
big-swipe-vs-card-scroll feel is the residual).

**D5 (P4, new): the Context sheet reopens scrolled below the chip row.** After a back/ESC
dismissal, the next sheet render frequently shows the chip row at `bounds=[0,0][0,0]` while
STALE pixels of the chips remain composited — taps at the pixel positions are dead (they are
below the sheet's current scroll fold), and only an in-sheet swipe re-materializes the row.
Cost two dead-end git-chip taps this pass before diagnosis. Fix direction: reset the sheet's
scroll position on open, and suppress the stale-frame composite (or accept + document).

Also recorded: automation "Run now" → `fault.mock.unscripted:runAutomationNow` (NEW mock arming
debt; the app sent the wire call and refreshed `listAutomations ok 9ms`; whether a snackbar
surfaced could not be confirmed before it expired — re-check when arming). Mock debts unchanged:
`git.getChanges`, `git.getCommitGraph`, `files.list`, generateCommitMessage, usage-stats channel.

## Part AR3 — rig notes for future passes

1. **IME-overlays-dump trap**: with the soft keyboard open, app buttons under the IME keep their
   PRE-IME bounds in the a11y dump while the IME window intercepts touches — taps at dump
   coordinates silently no-op. Always `keyevent 4` (or tap at the shifted bounds of the re-dump)
   before tapping buttons; dialogs shift up above the IME so their buttons stay visible.
2. **ESC (`keyevent 111`) wanders** — it dismissed the commit dialog AND the git pane this pass
   (known gotcha, now twice-confirmed on dialogs). `keyevent 4` dismisses the IME composing
   suggestion first (needs a second press).
3. **`pm clear` + paste-pairing needs ~20-char chunks**: single-shot `input text` truncated a
   178-char pairing link at ~48 chars; ~20-char chunks with 1.2 s gaps landed 100% including the
   `%3D` and `\&` escapes. Field clear via MOVE_END (123) + per-char DEL (67) is strictly 1:1 —
   a device-side `for` loop (single adb round trip) is the fast way.
4. **The stale-relay port trap** fired again (BindException on relay start) — `pkill -f
   MockRelayMainKt` only, never by port (qemu NAT).
5. **Disk discipline worked**: pre-freeing 2.1 GB of stale REA JSONs before cold boot avoided the
   pass-16 disk-space FATAL; 7.1 Gi free at REA start.
6. **DB ground truth via run-as**: `adb shell run-as com.zcode.android.app sqlite3
   databases/zcode.db 'SELECT … FROM interactions'` resolves "was it really pending?" questions
   in one query — the pass-17 D3 adjudication was decided by it, not by logcat (the ZCODE-PAIR
   buffer rotates past the interesting window in ~10 min).

## Part AS4 — rig lessons for future passes

1. **Disabled Compose buttons report `bounds=[0,0][0,0]`** — a zero-bounds node is a DISABLED
   node until proven otherwise (the branch sheet's "Create & switch" flipped 0,0 → real bounds
   the moment the field had content). Don't diagnose D2-class inertness on a disabled control.
2. **Radio/switch rows have ~130px dead gaps between them** — tapping between two switches
   silently toggles nothing; always tap the node bounds, not the visual row.
3. **Rapid DEL bursts drop keys** (~150/195/48-burst attempts each left residue); the reliable
   field-clear is the ITERATIVE loop: 80-DEL rounds with a dump-verified length check between
   rounds until 0. Then a single verified chunk pass. Exact-length verification (178/178, no
   `\&`, ends-with check) is what turned the flaky paste-pairing leg deterministic.
4. **`%s` in `input text` is a SPACE, not a colon** — "03%s30" typed "03 30" (and the HH:MM
   field's red-border invalid state rendered for it); the literal colon passes through unescaped.
5. **`input keyevent 66` (IME action) commits and closes the keyboard WITHOUT dismissing the
   dialog** — safer than `keyevent 4` around full-screen dialog editors (which closed the branch
   sheet but spared the commit dialog — behavior differs per surface, so prefer 66).
6. **Screenshot-coordinate taps misfire**: screenshots are 923×1983, the device is 1080×2340 —
   ALWAYS tap from `uiautomator dump` bounds (two leg retries this pass were pure scale errors).
7. The relay-restart D1 probe needs the app FOREGROUND with an established connection to
   reproduce the pass-17 shape; a restart while backgrounded exercises the honest
   reconnect-timeout + lazy-resume path instead.

## Part AT4 — rig lessons for future passes

1. **Button-label substring taps can hit TEXT FIELDS**: the helper's `--tap "Commit"` matched
   the draft text "p19 rig commit" inside the message field and typed into it instead. Use
   exact-match (or per-class Button nodes) for dialog buttons.
2. **Dialog switches sit at the row's RIGHT EDGE** (~x=964 device px in the commit dialog) —
   label taps are dead gaps (the switch-row lesson, now confirmed for M3 Switch rows in
   dialogs, not just settings).
3. **`keyevent 111` (ESC) CLOSES the whole commit dialog** — around multi-line dialog fields
   prefer `keyevent 66` (IME action; inserts a newline in multiline fields — clean up with
   DEL) or never dismiss the keyboard at all (tap the switch directly; it sits above the IME).
4. **The screenshot scale trap fired AGAIN with `sips` reporting 1080 wide** — screencaps on
   this AVD intermittently come out 923×1983 regardless; the a11y-dump bounds remain the ONLY
   authoritative tap coordinates.
5. **`input text` chunk size ≤ ~20 chars is the deterministic recipe** (9 chunks, zero drifts,
   exact 178/178) — a 56-char first chunk truncated 34 chars mid-payload with a varying cut
   point, re-confirming the pass-18 rule.
6. **DB ground truth adjudicates mock-vs-app fast**: run-as sqlite3 on `conversation_rows`
   settled the seeded-row question in minutes (see AT2) — prefer it over log-only reasoning
   when a transcript row disagrees with an answered interaction.
7. The gen-1 relay link doubles as a STALE-LINK fixture for the fresh-install chain (any
   link >10 min old fires the guard deterministically) — no special arming needed.

## Part AU3 — rig lessons for future passes

1. **`adb shell` inside a `while read` loop EATS the pipe**: `tail | while read c; do adb
   shell input text "$c"; done` typed exactly ONE chunk because the first `adb shell` drains
   the loop's stdin (adb forwards local stdin to the device shell). Fix: `adb shell input
   text "$c" < /dev/null` per iteration. This, not chunk size, was this pass's fresh-install
   "drift".
2. **The a11y-dump text is XML-escaped**: `&` lands as `&amp;` (+3 chars per ampersand), so a
   raw length check against a 7-ampersand pairing link reads 196–198 "typed" for a correct
   178-char field. Unescape before comparing, or compare tails.
3. **`&` in typed chunks must be escaped** (`\&`) device-side or `input text` backgrounds the
   command at the first `&`.
4. **Dialog switches toggle ONLY at the row's right edge (~x=964)** — re-confirmed twice this
   pass (Include-unstaged and Commit-&-push toggles); label taps and track-center taps do
   nothing.
5. **The terminal-consent ENABLE switch is a ~143px clickable box LEFT of the label** (its
   container at `[231,861][374,993]`) — the row label and the far-right edge are both dead.
6. **The composer send is tap-hostile while a hook card pins + an attachment chip squeezes the
   layout**: the send button's a11y bounds exist (and even report `0,0` in some dumps) but the
   clickable area responds only after the snackbar dismisses and the composer re-docks; one
   stray tap landed on the queue's "Send now" instead (which receipted that family). Budget a
   snackbar-dismiss + fresh dump before composer sends.
7. **Screenshot paint vs a11y dump can offset by ~200–300 px on sheet screens** even when the
   PNG is 1080×2340 (header-verified). Dumps remain the only authoritative tap source; never
   tap from screenshot pixels on bottom-sheet screens.

## Part AU4 — pass-20 REA angle: the complete wire-verb plane diff

Method: the desktop's phone-remote surface is the `zcodeAgentService` object — extracted by
sweeping the asar for `zcodeAgentService.<member>` accesses (**31 verbs**), then each verb was
checked against the phone's consumed transport inventory (V4Plane/RelayTransport/
DirectTransport literals + TaskServiceClient/ViewerTools + Phase9Ports). The envelope-type
plane (`type:"…",payload:` dispatches) and the two literal `*V4` strings were swept too. All
counted against the unchanged asar digest `99e280fb90b626cc…`.

**Desktop verbs with NO phone consumer (new parity rows):**

- **P4 (desktop-AUTHOR family, now concrete): the plugin marketplace/management plane.**
  Five verbs — `addPluginMarketplace`, `updatePluginMarketplace`, `installPlugin`,
  `getPluginsOverview`, `getPluginReferenceCatalog` — plus a **247-key
  `settings.plugins.*` i18n surface**: per-plugin detail with component inventory
  (agent/command/hook/lsp/mcp/skill), **per-plugin config with SECRET management**
  (config.save / clearSecret / showSecret / hideSecret / sensitiveUnavailable /
  undoClearSecret / undoRestoreOption), **update checks** (checkForUpdates.found/.none),
  and **marketplace authoring** (Choose directory, drag-and-drop hint, Validate marketplace,
  `exportMarketplaceSourceArchive`). The phone consumes exactly `listPlugins` (read-only,
  GAP-7) + `setPluginEnabled` (the enable toggle) + the skills catalog. Every installation/
  update/configure/secret/marketplace-management flow is desktop-author only.
- **P4: session close-without-delete.** The desktop session chips expose a **"Close session"
  button** (`closeSession`); the phone's task menu has archive / delete / rename / continue
  (`continueTask` is the Resume wire) but **no close** semantic.
- **P4-smallest: on-demand compact.** `compactSession` exists with a desktop UI caller
  (taskId/workspacePath + inputId bookkeeping); the phone has no compact surface (consistent
  with pass-18's "autoCompact display-only both sides" — the desktop can compact a session on
  demand, the phone cannot).
- **Ledger sub-note (usage-dashboard depth, still rig-blocked):** the per-task token-usage
  wire verb is `getTaskTokenUsage` (desktop-only; the phone's usage port is app-level
  `getAppUsageStats` + the coding-plan snapshot family). When the mock arms the usage-stats
  channel, this is the verb a per-task depth view would ride.
- **P4-smallest (form-factor row, G31 class): the desktop file-tree browser.** A `FileTree`
  component appears 111× with `openFile` call sites; the phone's Files surface is the
  per-file viewer family (`files.list/readText/binaryPreview/share/download` + attachments +
  mentions) — a mobile minimum, deliberately not a tree.

**Explicit non-findings (so future passes don't miscount):** `sendConfigCasCommandV4` /
`sendHostCasCommandV4` are internal FUNCTION names wrapping `sendConversationCommandV4`
CAS-of-config envelopes (config snapshots / host control), not wire verbs or gaps;
`syncAppRuntimePreferences` (runtime-preference propagation to workspace clients),
`onDynamicCuaPermissionObservation` / `onDynamicSessionEvent` /
`onDynamicSessionRuntimePreferencesRequest` / `respondSessionRuntimePreferences`, and
`dispose*`/`initialize` are desktop-internal lifecycle plumbing. **No permission-policy gap
exists in either direction**: the desktop has NO allow/deny rules editor either —
`toolDenylist` (carried in session snapshots) is the only policy knob on both sides, and the
phone consumes snapshots passively.

**Phone verbs re-confirmed present desktop-side (the diff's positive half):** all 143
phone-side entries resolve to desktop implementations — the conversation family
(`subscribe/initialize/resyncConversationV4`, `helloConversationV4`, rows/attachments),
the command envelope family (`sendConversationCommandV4` with 12 asar sites), the mode/
thought/model trajectory (`setMode` + `switchCollaborationMode` + `setThoughtLevel`), the
files family (`readTextFile/readFileRange/readBinaryPreview/searchWorkspaceFiles`), the git
family incl. checkpoints and the write tier, the terminal family, the automations family,
the tasks family, MCP/plugins/skills/subagents/providers/bots/codingplan status families,
and `getView`. **The phone consumes every phone-relevant verb the desktop offers except the
four families above — the plane is closed.**

## Part AV3 — NEW app-side findings

- **F-21-A (P3) — the conversation screen's touch input goes fully DEAD after heavy
  scrolling, cleared only by re-navigation.** Reproduction shape: after ~40 fling
  gestures reaching the timeline top, the list stops scrolling; then EVERY touch on the
  conversation screen is dead — list, the scroll-to-bottom FAB, even the header's
  Context chip — while KEY events still work (BACK navigated out with
  `nav.screen :: route=tasks`) and hub touches still work. Evidence: pixel-identical
  screenshots across three distinct gestures (cmp-verified), FAB tap pixel-identical,
  Context chip tap pixel-identical, then BACK navigating. Wire stayed healthy
  (heartbeats every 8s) throughout. Re-entering the task restores normal input. Not the
  recorded pending-card freeze class — no card was rendered at freeze time. Needs a code
  look at the conversation screen's pointer-input/interaction plumbing (candidate
  neighborhood: the freeze-gate's blocked-state propagation or an a11y/virtualization
  interaction consuming the pointer stream).
- **GAP-21-A (P3) — @-mentions are DEAD for a first-token mention, wire-proofed.**
  `WriteComponents.kt:796` computes the trigger as
  `state.draft.substringAfterLast(' ', "")` — Kotlin returns the **missing default**
  when the draft contains NO space, so a draft that STARTS with the mention (`@read`)
  computes `atToken = ""` and the mention menu can never appear. Live A/B on the rig:
  draft `@read` → **zero** `searchWorkspaceFiles` wire calls, no panel; draft
  `x @read` (space-delimited) → **7** `file.searchWorkspaceFiles` channel calls and the
  panel renders the seeded `README.md` hit. The most natural mention shape — starting a
  message with a file reference — is unreachable. Fix direction:
  `substringAfterLast(' ', missing = draft)` (token = whole draft when no space).
- **Papercut (P4): the queue strip's Auto-send label lags one toggle behind.** Tapping
  Auto-send fires `sendConversationCommandV4 ok` (51ms) but "· paused" only drops on the
  NEXT toggle; observed both directions (the switch state itself follows the wire).
- **Papercut (P4): the mention panel does not re-trigger for the same token** after a
  pick/miss cycle — `LaunchedEffect(atToken)` is keyed on the token VALUE, so re-typing
  the identical token (state returned to a token it already searched) leaves stale
  empty `mentionHits` until the token changes. Same neighborhood as GAP-21-A; fix both

## Part AV4 — mock arming debt CLOSED (F-21-B): the Files viewer could never have data

The Files viewer (§23.4 phase-9 plane: `files.list` → `file.readdir`) degraded
honestly on every prior pass because the MOCK never armed it:

1. `seedWorkspaceFiles` (RIG-2, G9) only registered the file PATHS as bare keys for the
   `searchWorkspaceFiles` @-mention filter — no directory listings existed, so
   `readdir(<root>)` always faulted `fault.file.notFound`.
2. Even with listings, the phone requests **absolute workspace paths**
   (`workspaceRoot = /synthetic/ws-one`) while the seeded tree is workspace-relative.

Fixed in `tools/mockzcode` (rig code, not app code): `seedWorkspaceFiles` now builds a
real directory tree (root listing + nested dirs + typed entries), and the file-channel
handlers (`readdir`/`stat`/`readTextFile`/`readFileRange`) resolve workspace-relative
views of absolute paths via a shared `fileRelPath` helper; `MockRelayMain` also seeds
paged README.md content for the viewer leg. Four new self-tests pin the tree shape
(`MockZCodeFileTreeSeedingSelfTest`: root children, nested dirs, typed entries +
search keys preserved, no duplicate children); `:tools:mockzcode:test` + `jar` BUILD
SUCCESSFUL. The Part AV2 Files receipts are the payoff — the pass-20 REA classification
of the FileTree browser as "desktop-only form-factor row" needs a correction: the PHONE
SHIPS a read-only workspace file browser (it was simply never rig-armed), and with data
armed it browses/navigates/reads exactly per §23.4/INV-9/INV-16.

## Part AZ5 — REA pass-25 dig (deeper than pass 24: the client-capability handshake + the sendText envelope schema, from the shipped chunks)

Extracted from the asar (asar-spec offsets, data base 7,087,308): `/out/host/index.js`
(1,498,022 B), `/out/main/index.js` (735,396 B), and the two host chunks that carry the
protocol: `/out/host/chunk-LNGNUNBX.js` (113,415 B — the V4 plane/schema chunk) and
`/out/host/chunk-4RHDQOPX.js` (the pendingInteraction/tool-vocabulary chunk). The
conversation-command vocabulary does NOT live in zcode.cjs (0 hits) — it lives in the host
chunks; zcode.cjs is the CLI/agent kernel.

- **G48 (NEW P3 — the pass headline): the phone never declares `capabilities` in its
  clientHello → the desktop's workflow-run DELTA streaming is never enabled → the phone's
  continuous ~8s `conversationWorkflowRunsV4` polling (pass-23's 291-calls/40min WATCH
  observation) is the visible symptom.** Chain: desktop clientHelloSchema strict-parses
  `capabilities:{workspaceHookReviewUi?,workflowRunDeltas?}`; `clientSupportsWorkflowRunDeltas
  = capabilities?.workflowRunDeltas === true` gates the delta stream; the relay's
  forwardedConnection forwards the bit ONLY when the client declared it
  (`...c.workflowRunDeltas===true?{workflowRunDeltas:!0}:{}`); the HOST's createHello declares
  `workflowRunDeltas:!0` toward clients. Phone side: `ClientHello.capabilities` EXISTS
  (V4Wire.kt:110-117, "declared only per the one-way rules") but its ONLY construction site
  (V4Plane.kt:637-643, initializeV4) omits it — the phone even DECODES the host's
  `workflowRunDeltas` bit (HostCapabilities) and ignores it. Remedy: declare
  `{workflowRunDeltas:true}` + consume the delta stream with the existing delta machinery.
  The mock never enforces the gate — the rig cannot catch this; production-only behavioral
  delta (wasteful polling + slower run updates vs the desktop's pushes).
- **G49 (NEW P4-small): per-send `requestedDelivery` ("startNow"|"queue"|"guide")** — the
  phone's CommandCoordinator supports the key (CommandCoordinator.kt:104/123) but ZERO
  feature-layer/UI senders exist: the phone routes sends purely by the session's routing
  mode; the desktop's sendText schema allows a per-message delivery request (the "send this
  one NOW even though the session queues" override).
- **G50 (NEW P4-small): `heldQueueDisposition` ("clearQueueAndSend"|"keepQueueAndSend") +
  `expectedHeldQueueItemIds` CAS** — plumbed VM→port (ConversationViewModel.send
  (heldQueueDisposition), default null) but NO UI caller ever sets it: the send-into-held-
  queue CHOICE (clear vs keep) never surfaces on the phone. The desktop's sendGoalCommand
  carries the same pair.

   `V7e = /(^|[\s\p{Script=Han}\u3000-\u303f\uff00-\uffef])(@)([^\s/@$#¥￥]*)$/u`; invalidation
   when the preceding char is Han AND the query is dotted (`U7e=\p{Script=Han}`, `H7e=/\S\.\S/`);
   `¥/￥` normalize to `$`. The file-search hook enables on parsed trigger `@` && !disabled; it

   gitignore-aware filtering (`workspace-file-ignore`,

Scope: full emulation walk with NEW verification axes no prior pass measured (cold/warm

apps, bundled glm plugins, shipped config) plus new renderer censuses (the complete i18n
