## Part BC.1 — NEW verification axes (measured for the first time in 31 passes)

1. **Startup timing (`am start -W`)**: COLD ×3 = 1,939 ms / 1,343 ms / 1,542 ms / 1,390 ms
   (first-launch 1.94 s, steady cold ~1.4 s); HOT (HOME→relaunch) ×3 = 383/549/612 ms.
   On the 8 GB emulator under swiftshader this is healthy; no `reportFullyDrawn` call
   exists in the app (measurement = ActivityTaskManager "Displayed"; the baselineprofile
   module exists but `StartupBenchmark` measures startup without an app-reported
   fully-drawn signal — P4 polish: `activity.reportFullyDrawn()` after the first tasks
   frame would sharpen both the macrobenchmark and Macrobenchmark-derived baseline
   profiles).
2. **Scroll jank (gfxinfo framestats)**: 6-fling sweep on the conversation timeline =
   90 frames, 100% janky, p50 93 ms / p90 200 ms — BUT the same sweep on the system
   Settings app on the SAME emulator measured p50 125 ms / p90 200-250 ms: the
   swiftshader software-GL emulator is the bottleneck, not the app (the app is BETTER
   than system Settings on p50). No on-device (real-GPU) verdict possible from this
   rig; the campaign's first jank numbers are recorded as environment-relative only.
   `Number Slow issue draw commands: 90/90` = the software renderer, not app draw cost.
3. **Memory footprint**: after the full walk, TOTAL PSS 98 MB / RSS 214 MB / VmHWM
   228 MB, 36 threads, 1 Activity, 5 AppContexts, 0 WebViews, 0 Death Recipients —
   lean and clean (threads are DefaultDispatcher/TaskRunner classes, no leaks visible
   in the thread table).
4. **Process-death restore**: draft typed → `am kill` (process killed, pid gone) →
   relaunch COLD 1,534 ms → auto-reconnect → the SAME conversation reopened via task
   selection and the draft "draft31pd" RESTORED in the composer. The persisted-draft
   contract survives process death (previously only kill-survival was claimed).
5. **Config-change recreation matrix** (the campaign's first systematic sweep):
   - **Night mode** (`cmd uimode night yes`): conversation, tasks, context sheet, all
     dialogs re-rendered correctly (screenshots 14/16); nav-bar scrim painted by the
     system (the pass-2 enableEdgeToEdge contract holds).
   - **Font scale 1.3** (`settings put system font_scale 1.3`): conversation + tasks
     legible, no crush (the recorded "font-1.3 crush" ledger small did NOT reproduce;
     pass-15 line 327 stands). A11y findings at 1.3 (see BC.4).
   - **Display size Largest** (`wm density 572`, ~1.3×): the queue strip's per-row
     buttons wrapped to two lines ("Del/ete") but stayed tappable; session bar, pinned
     card, composer all intact; the A11/GAP-A16 height budgets held at the extreme
     scale (screenshot 17).
   - **Landscape** (user_rotation 1): conversation renders session bar + queue strip +
     composer without clipping (the A11 fixed budget visible live); NO landscape crash
     anywhere in the walk.
   - **Every uiMode flip recreates the Activity** (wm_relaunch_resume ×5 + 6
     onDestroy/isFinishing=false + onCreate/savedInstanceState=true cycles): the app
     survived each recreation with the hub process intact — BUT the recreation count
     exposed the pass-5-recorded design fact that AppContainer is rebuilt per Activity
     (6 recreations → 7 Activities / 19 AppContexts in dumpsys; Post-GC 18 AppContexts,
     PSS back to 126 MB, no unbounded growth, but the context count is the price of
     the no-Application-class design — WATCH, not a defect: numbers plateau, memory
     does not).
6. **Forced doze** (`dumpsys battery unplug` + `deviceidle force-idle`, 100 s
   backgrounded): heartbeats STOP (0 in doze — WorkManager/alarms deferred as designed),
   the reconnect ladder kept advancing (6 attempts, intervals growing ~12s→21s→20s→40s),
   hub degraded honestly to DEGRADED; on wake + foreground, CONNECTED in ~2 s with
   `relay.recovered :: subscriptions=1 snapshotReplace=true`. The doze contract holds.
7. **Monkey stress** (first time in the campaign): seed 3131 injected 771/1500 events

   NOT the app; the app process survived and stayed interactive); seed 4242 injected
   **1,200/1,200 events, Monkey finished, app process unchanged**. Total 1,971 random
   events, **zero app FATALs, zero app ANRs** across the whole pass.
8. **A11y tree audits** (`uiautomator` walk: unlabeled clickables / sub-48dp targets /
   zero-bounds):
   - Tasks home (1.0×): 0 unlabeled, 1 small ("+ New task" 108×23dp at the nav-bar

## Part BC.6 — the static find that upgrades F-27-B (recorded with its sweep method)

A new repo-wide sweep (tools-quality one-off, /tmp/p31/dropped_args.py: for every
fun whose defaulted params are null/empty-lambda, find call sites that omit an
in-scope same-named param) over features/ + app/src/main + core/ui returned EXACTLY
TWO hits, both in ConversationScreen.kt:
- `ConversationScreen → TimelineBody(...) DROPS onOpenAttachment,
  onOpenAttachmentExternally, onSectionCrash` (line 552) — the L7 diagnostics seam
  is dropped at the SAME hop: a timeline grouping crash still renders the error
  card + Retry (the boundary works) but the stack never reaches
  `diagnosticsStore.writeCrash("conversation-timeline", …)` — the L7 contract is
  half-wired (the boundary catches, the seam is null).
- `TimelineBody → TimelineRow(...) DROPS onOpenAttachment,
  onOpenAttachmentExternally, rewindPreviewProvider` (line 1047) — **F-27-B's root
  cause** (preview structurally unreachable from timeline rows) AND the G28 fix
  regression: the zoom viewer + external handoff callbacks (817318be) are dropped
  at the same hop, so **the G28 live receipt's "AttachmentsViewerUiTest passes"
  never applied to the real timeline** — tapping an inbound image thumbnail in the
  shipped app does nothing (live-confirmed this pass: tap on the mock.png
  thumbnail at its painted bounds → zero wires, byte-identical screen, no viewer
  dialog). G28 was marked SHIPPED on the strength of row-level pins
  (AttachmentViewerUiTest hosts YouBlock directly with the callbacks passed);
  the screen-level wiring was never pinned. **F-27-B's fix is now a 3-line
  forward + a screen-level pin**; the same commit should forward all five dropped
  params (the 3 at :552 + 3 at :1047, two overlapping) and add
  TimelineWiringContractTest asserting ConversationScreen forwards every
  callback param to TimelineBody and TimelineBody forwards to TimelineRow (a
  structural pin, or reflection-based param-name diff).

## Part BE.2 — NEW defects (ordered by severity; every one reproduced, root-caused, cited)

### F-33-A (P2) — the ZOMBIE CONVERSATION SCREEN after any Activity recreate

**Symptom.** After a configuration-change recreate while a conversation is open, the screen
still renders normally ("Connected · Completed", cards, queue), but **every action on it is
dead**: queue Delete, Keep waiting and composer Send produced **ZERO log lines and ZERO
wires** (controlled leg CFG3/CFG4, 12:14–12:15, stable relay, no gen swap: dark mode `yes`
→ recreate → three actions → nothing; the draft stays in the composer). Control: Back →
re-open the same task → the SAME actions fire at once (snooze `ok in 42ms`, delete `ok in
32ms`). When the old container's transport was mid-recovery at recreate time, the dead
screen does worse: the status chip froze at "Reconnecting…" while the NEW hub was
CONNECTED, and Allow once FAILED on the destroyed connection —
`sendConversationCommandV4 failed: channel closed: abnormal close 1006: Software caused
connection abort` (connectionId=relay-21, the abort text of the OLD socket from 12:03:17,
answered at 12:08:08 — leg SPLIT1). The retained screen's workflow-runs ticker likewise
fails `server close 1000` at every recreate (6 occurrences, each at a recreate instant).

**Root cause (exact).** `MainActivity.kt:128` builds the WHOLE graph per Activity
(`container = AppContainer(this)` — hub, transport, ports); `ZCodeApp.kt:570-579`
`rememberConversationViewModel` keeps the VM in a `ConversationVmHolder` ViewModel —
retained across configuration changes by design — and returns `holder.vm ?:
ConversationViewModel(container.conversationPort, …)`: after a recreate the holder already
holds a VM bound to the DESTROYED container's port, so the new container is silently
ignored by the screen that is on display.

**Triggers observed this pass:** dark-mode flip (`cmd uimode night`), **Battery Saver's
forced dark theme** (applied at the next foreground — the realistic field trigger, along
with the automatic sunset dark-mode schedule), the navigation-mode overlay switch
(gesture ↔ 3-button), and Display-size changes (`wm density`); pass 31 already showed font
scale and locale recreate. `configChanges` covers only
`keyboardHidden|orientation|screenLayout|screenSize` (REA manifest decode, BE.4) —
rotation is safe. Split-screen entry from Recents did NOT recreate on API 30 (minimized
dock) — corrected attribution, see BE.6.

**F-27-A link (hypothesis, evidence recorded).** After the SPLIT1 failure, the re-entered
screen showed the exact F-27-A face: the gen-4 approval card live, Allow once → "Already
handled on the desktop." with zero wires, Room lifecycle `STALE` for
`mock-p33-gen4-49ffc7`. This pass cannot separate the two contributing events (the failed
stale-bound answer and pass 31's in-process relay gen swap both occurred), but F-33-A is a
deterministic generator of the "card alive, answers dead" face that F-27-A has chased for
six passes. **Recommendation: fix F-33-A first, then re-run the F-27-A trigger set.**

**Fix direction.** Hoist `AppContainer` to process scope (an `Application` subclass or a
process-level holder) — this single change also removes F-33-B, F-33-C and the per-recreate
reconnect; at minimum, re-bind the holder when `container.conversationPort` identity changes.
Pin: a Robolectric `ActivityScenario.recreate()` test asserting that a queue delete issued
AFTER recreate reaches the live port.

### F-33-B (P3, heap-proven leak) — every recreated Activity + its whole AppContainer is retained for the process lifetime

`am dumpheap` (forces a full GC) → hprof-conv → a custom HPROF walker (BE.6): after four
recreates there are **5 MainActivity, 5 AppContainer, 5 ConnectionHub, 5 RelayTransport,
5 DiagnosticsFileStore, 16 OkHttpClient, 15 okhttp3.Dispatcher** live instances (one
RealWebSocket — the old sockets are closed, the graphs are not). The retention path,
byte-exact from the dump:

`static java.lang.Thread.defaultUncaughtExceptionHandler` → `MainActivity$$ExternalSyntheticLambda0@0x13085a08{f$0 = MainActivity#5, f$1 →}` → `Lambda0@…9d0{f$0 = MainActivity#4, f$1 →}` → `…9e0{#3}` → `…9f0{#2}` → `…a00{f$0 = MainActivity#1, f$1 = RuntimeInit$KillApplicationHandler}`

`MainActivity.kt:123-127` installs a NEW default handler in every `onCreate`, chaining the
previous one (`platformHandler = Thread.getDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler()`) and closing
over `this` (for `container.diagnosticsStore`). This upgrades pass 31's "7 Activities /
18-19 AppContexts post-GC = WATCH" to a proven leak with its exact path; PSS read
98 MB at the pass-31 baseline and 176 MB after this session's four recreates (201 MB right
after the heap dump itself); threads stayed flat (36 → 38). Fix: install the handler once per process (static guard or the
`Application` hoist) and point it at a process-scoped diagnostics store.

### F-33-C (P3) — a recreate is treated as a BACKGROUND ENTRY: approval notifications re-alert while the user is in the app

`MainActivity.kt:291-295` calls `container.notifications.onBackground()` in every `onStop`,
including the configuration-change stop. Receipt (NIGHT1, app in the FOREGROUND): dark
`yes` → `notify.repost … (background entry)` → onDestroy → onCreate →
`notify.show :: key=interaction:mock-approva channel=permissions` (the HIGH channel:
sound + vibrate) → `NotificationService: Muting recently noisy 0|com.zcode.android.app…`;
dark `no` → the same again. Session totals: 19 reposts, 12 shows, **17 system
"recently noisy" mutes**; Android's own Settings now estimates the Approvals channel at
"~102 notifications per day". Each recreate also runs a FULL reconnect (UNPAIRED →
AUTHENTICATING → CONNECTED, 1.3–2.5 s). Fix: skip `onBackground/onForeground` when
`isChangingConfigurations` (structurally: the F-33-A hoist).

### F-33-D (P3) — the IME double inset + the GAP-A16 composer squeeze re-manifest

`ConversationScreen.kt:274-279` applies `.padding(inner)` (the M3 Scaffold's default
content insets, which include the navigation bar) and then `.imePadding()` without
`consumeWindowInsets(inner)` — with the keyboard up, the navigation-bar inset is applied
TWICE. Measured on the painted frame: the gap between the composer box and the keyboard
top is **145 px under 3-button navigation (132 px bar + 13 px padding) and 60 px under
gesture navigation (44 px bar + 16 px)**, versus 16 px with the keyboard down; the math
reproduces exactly (gesture: 44 + 817 IME = 861 → box bottom 1479, composer bottom 1463).
Under a tall pinned stack this dead band is what pushes the composer's action row out of
paint: **two organic repros** this pass (hook-review card + queue strip + background
banner + shared-context chip at 10:26; approval card + the same strips at 11:56, which also
swallowed the first dead-zone send) — the field text clipped
at its top, the attach and **Send buttons not painted**, a tap at Send's a11y centre sends
nothing; closing the keyboard restores the row. GAP-A16's closure (`dbca4ad8`, pass-13
receipt "composer draft at y=1244–1376") verified the FIELD's bounds only — the Send
button was never checked in paint. One-line fix: `.padding(inner).consumeWindowInsets(inner)
.imePadding()`; re-pin `ComposerSqueezeBudgetTest` on the Send button's painted bounds with
synthetic nav + IME insets.

### F-33-E (P3) — the pending count disagrees across four surfaces (STALE leaks into two of them)

Simultaneous truth (12:33): Room `interactions` = 2 DISPLAYED (1 permission, 1 question) +
2 STALE + 5 RESOLVED. The surfaces: **bell badge 4 and the Approvals inbox lists 4** —
`observeOpen` is `resolvedAtMs IS NULL` (`Daos.kt:108`), which includes STALE, so a 19-hour-
old pass-31 STALE approval is offered with Allow once / Deny; **the widget says "Nothing
needs you"** — it counts UNSEEN broker records only (`PendingApprovalsWidget.kt:160`), so two
genuinely open interactions the user has viewed vanish from it; **the shade re-posts a
persisted record for a STALE interaction** — `notification_records.pb` still holds
`interaction:mock-p31-gen3-c5bc6f` (STALE since 2026-11-06), re-posted as "ZCode needs your
approval" on every background entry today, because `StoreDiffs.closedInteractions`
(`StoreDiffs.kt:67`) is `previousIds − openNow` with `previousIds` empty at process start —
a record whose interaction closed before the current process can never be dismissed.
Fix: one shared "open" predicate (open lifecycle AND not STALE) for badge, inbox, widget
and broker; seed `previousIds` from the broker's loaded attention keys on the first
snapshot.

### F-33-F (P3, privacy) — the clipboard is read on EVERY conversation open

`WriteComponents.kt:868` runs `LaunchedEffect(Unit) { pasteImage = clipboardHasImage(context) }`
and `clipboardImageUri` (`:1260-1262`) calls `cm.primaryClip` — the full clip DATA, not the
description. Receipt: `appops READ_CLIPBOARD` access time reset to 3 s and then 2 s after two
consecutive conversation opens (it read 7 min before). On Android 12+ (Ernest's S23) each
read of another app's clip shows the system "pasted from your clipboard" toast; the app
also pulls whatever was copied (passwords included) into its process to inspect a MIME type.
Fix: probe `cm.primaryClipDescription` (no data, no toast); read the clip only on the Paste
tap.

### F-33-G (P3, honesty) — with notifications blocked by Android, the app still says they are on

Settings → Apps → ZCode → notifications OFF (AppSettings `importance=NONE`, shade cleared).
The app's Notifications section still shows **Approval requests ON, Task finished / failed
ON, Connection lost ON**, with no warning anywhere (Tasks screen, conversation, Settings);
the broker keeps "posting" into the void (`AndroidNotificationSink` documents "degrade
silently at the SYSTEM level"). For a remote-approval companion, silently lost approval
alerts are the worst failure mode. Fix: check `areNotificationsEnabled()` + the
permissions channel's importance on resume; show a warning row with a deep link to
`ACTION_APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS` (and the API-33 runtime-denial state). Note: on API 30
the `POST_NOTIFICATION` app-op is NOT enforced (posts went through with `ignore`) — the
system toggle is the real block.

### F-33-H (P3, safety) — blind approve from the shade

`NotificationPlan.kt:14-20`: approval/question notifications are category-only at BOTH
content levels ("ZCode needs your approval", `android.text=null`, `vis=PRIVATE`), yet the
same notification carries **Approve / Deny** actions — so a shell command can be approved
from the shade without ever seeing it. The desktop's own notification shows the subject
(`notification.command` "Command: {command}" / `notification.file` "File: {paths}", BE.5.3)
and has no action buttons. Fix: keep the lock-screen PUBLIC version category-only
(`setPublicVersion`), and give the private (unlocked) version the tool + command line when
the user picked "Task titles"; or require the app for Bash-class approvals.

### F-27-C (P3) — re-manifested with a dead tap that performs BACK

The Context sheet opened half-expanded with its "Open" footer below the fold: under
3-button navigation the "Model calls / Share" chip row is painted UNDER the nav bar
(y ≈ 2249 inside the bar's `[0,2208][1080,2340]` frame; the ◀ glyph overdraws "Share"), and a
tap on "Share" hit the system **Back** key (the sheet dismissed; the next tap landed on the
composer's +). Under gesture navigation the same footer is cut by the screen edge until the
sheet is dragged up. Fix: inset the footer by `navigationBars` and include it in the
partially-expanded height (or `skipPartiallyExpanded`).

### P4 smalls (new)

- **N-BE-1 (automation time semantics)**: the editor's time hint reads "HH:MM (24h, local)"
  (`features/tasks/.../strings.xml:66`), but the cron runs on the DESKTOP clock and the
  bootstrap carries no desktop timezone; a phone in another zone writes the wrong hour.
  Live: phone switched to Asia/Tokyo — "Daily at 02:00" unchanged (desktop-local, unlabeled).
  Relative labels and row clocks re-rendered correctly without a restart ("AGENT 8:08 PM").
- **N-BE-2 (outbox retention)**: `OutboxDao` (`Daos.kt:128-147`) has no delete query —
  terminal rows (ACKED / FAILED_STALE / EXPIRED) are kept forever with their full payloads

  keyboard's Enter inserts a newline and there is no Ctrl/Cmd+Enter — no way to send from a
  DeX / tablet / Chromebook keyboard (the desktop's `composerSend` binding).
- **N-BE-4 (notice colour)**: `WriteComponents.kt:1223/1227` paint the send-notice text and
  its ✕ in `onErrorContainer` for EVERY kind — the INFO success "Trusted 2 hook(s) — the
  session continues." and "Already handled on the desktop." render in error red on the

  85 library locales, x86/x86_64 native libs, `descriptor.proto` packaged.

1. **Gesture navigation**: the nav bar becomes 44 px; every non-sheet surface insets

   `navigation_mode=0` — recorded).
2. **Hardware-keyboard traversal**: TAB walks header → workspace chips → automation verbs →

   logical order with the list auto-scrolling to the focus; DPAD focus + ENTER activate
   (session-config chip focused; DPAD_UP + ENTER = Back). Reachability passes.
3. **Timezone change** (Europe/Dublin → Asia/Tokyo live): no crash, no recreate; relative
   times stayed right; absolute row clocks re-rendered in JST.
4. **At-rest audit** (run-as pull of all 13 private files): the pairing secret appears in
   NONE of them (no base64, no raw 32-byte form) — `credential_envelope.pb` holds a Tink
   keyset (`vault.keyset.v1`) + `credential.secret.v1` ciphertext, plus plaintext metadata
   (deviceSid / mid / origin / desktop name — identifiers, not secrets); diagnostics logs
   carry `"nonce":"[REDACTED]"`; datastores live in `no_backup/`. The Room DB is plaintext
   (conversation rows, drafts, interaction payloads incl. tool commands) under the app
   sandbox + FBE — posture note, not a defect.
5. **Network impairment** (host proxy `netproxy.py`, BE.6): at 400 ms one-way + 8 KB/s the
   reconnect ran RECONNECTING → CONNECTED in 10.5 s and a conversation subscribe took 3.2 s.
   A 2.7-min dead zone (bytes held, sockets open): loss detected in 24 s (OkHttp ping/pong
   20 s), reconnect attempts backed off (10–30 s), a send during it was refused honestly
   ("You're offline — the draft is saved on this phone. Reconnect to send.",
   `command.blockedOffline`, nothing journaled), recovery 16 s after release
   (`relay.recovered subscriptions=3 snapshotReplace=true`), and the re-send landed
   **exactly once** (one outbox row, ACKED, attempts=1). Design note: the phone never
   auto-sends an offline draft — a deliberate no-surprise-send choice.
6. **Power restrictions** (Battery Saver + RESTRICTED standby bucket + background
   restriction + Data Saver): the background socket aborted at once and the reconnect
   ladder went silent (OS-enforced); foreground recovery to CONNECTED in 2.5 s — then
   F-33-A struck (above).
7. **High-contrast text**: outlined coloured text, all screens legible. **Forced RTL**:
   the UI stays LTR by recorded design (`supportsRtl` OFF + the `RtlLocaleGateTest`
   tripwire; both shipped locales are LTR) — confirmed, no half-mirrored layouts.
8. **Split-screen** via Recents works (top pane; heads-up Approve/Deny posted on the way).
9. **Tablet geometry** (1600×2560 / 2560×1600 @ 320 dpi): everything renders and stays
   usable — see G61 for what is missing.

## Part BE.6 — rig recipes recorded for the next pass

- **`adb root` / `unroot` restarts adbd and kills a host-side `adb logcat` capture**;
  restart it, and recover gaps with `adb logcat -d -t '<MM-DD HH:MM:SS.mmm>'`. rig.py's
  `since` falls back to the START of the file when a marker is missing — that produced one
  false "split-screen recreates" attribution this pass, corrected from the ring buffer.
  Always confirm the marker line exists before trusting a `since` slice.
- **The emulator console's `network delay/speed` does not shape traffic to 10.0.2.2**
  (ping RTT stayed 0.3 ms under gprs/gsm). Use the host proxy: relay on 18102
  (`MOCK_PORT=18102 /tmp/p33/relay2.sh <gen>`), `DELAY_MS=… RATE_BPS=… python3
  /tmp/p33/netproxy.py` on 18100; `touch /tmp/p33/blackhole` holds bytes with sockets open
  (dead zone), removing it flushes them.
- **Heap retention paths**: `am dumpheap <pid>` (forces a GC) → `hprof-conv` →
  `/tmp/p33/hprof_paths.py <hprof> <class-substring>` (referrers + GC roots),
  `hprof_fields.py <hprof> <exact class>` (captured fields), `hprof_count.py` (exact-class
  instance counts). `kill -10` is refused for app pids on this image.
- **After ANY recreate, leave and re-open the conversation before driving actions**
  (F-33-A) — otherwise taps are silent no-ops and look like rig flakiness.
- uiautomator's app bounds stop at y=2072 (`DisplayInfo app=1080x2072`); with the field at
  1902–2056 the painted Send centre is ≈ (960, 2117). Crop painted truth with
  `sips -c <h> <w> --cropOffset <y> 0` (no Pillow on this machine).
- Split-screen on API 30: Recents (`KEYCODE_APP_SWITCH`) → swipe the card to centre → tap its
  icon → "Split screen"; `am start --windowingMode 3` does not split here.
- Notification blocking on API 30 = Settings → app notifications toggle
  (`am start -a android.settings.APP_NOTIFICATION_SETTINGS --es
  android.provider.extra.APP_PACKAGE <pkg>`); the `POST_NOTIFICATION` app-op is not enforced.
- Navigation mode: `cmd overlay enable|disable com.android.internal.systemui.navbar.gestural`
  (recreates the app — remember F-33-A).

## Part BE.7 — pass-33 verdict and ledger delta

On the byte-identical APK (`9084b920…` debug, `335e75e0…` release, desktop `99e280fb…`) the
companion passed its smoke matrix end-to-end and held on most new axes (keyboard traversal,
live timezone change, at-rest secret sealing, latency/bandwidth/dead-zone resilience with
exactly-once delivery, power restrictions, high contrast, RTL-by-design, split-screen,
tablet rendering), and the release artifact reverses clean (R8, no mock code, platform
no-cleartext). The new axes broke the two-pass "saturation" streak with **one P2, seven
P3s, a P3 re-manifest and six new G rows**:

- **F-33-A (P2)** zombie conversation screen after any recreate (retained VM bound to the
  destroyed per-Activity container) — a deterministic generator of the F-27-A face;
- **F-33-B (P3)** heap-proven Activity + AppContainer leak via the chained
  uncaught-exception handler (retention path byte-exact);
- **F-33-C (P3)** recreate = background entry → approval re-alerts in the foreground (17
  system noisy-mutes) + a full reconnect per recreate;
- **F-33-D (P3)** IME double inset (132 px / 44 px dead band) + the GAP-A16 Send-unpainted
  re-manifest (closure was bounds-only);
- **F-33-E (P3)** pending-count incoherence (badge/inbox count STALE; widget counts unseen;
  a day-old STALE record re-posts forever);
- **F-33-F (P3)** clipboard data read on every conversation open;
- **F-33-G (P3)** system-blocked notifications invisible in-app;
- **F-33-H (P3)** blind shade approve (category-only text + Approve/Deny actions);
- **F-27-C (P3) re-manifest** — a footer tap that performs system Back;
- **G61–G66** (adaptive large-screen layout; desktop keep-awake visibility; idle-time outcome
  notifications; CUA permission observation [P3]; mention taxonomy; typed error card);
- **N-BE-1…6** smalls (automation "local" time, outbox retention, hardware-keyboard send,
  notice colour, APK size, mock debts).

**Fix-round opener order (supersedes BD.6):** F-33-A (process-scoped AppContainer — also
closes F-33-B, F-33-C and the per-recreate reconnect; then re-test F-27-A) → F-33-D (one
line) → F-27-B (the 3-line forwards) → F-33-E + F-27-A → F-33-G + F-33-H → F-33-F → F-27-C →
GAP-21-A (+ G65) → G64 → N-BC / N-BD / N-BE smalls → G48 + G51 → G60–G63, G66.

**On par / better:** the phone already beats the desktop on notification actions,
grouping and privacy levels, the glance widget, launcher shortcuts, hardware-keyboard
reachability, exactly-once offline handling and having zero telemetry; parity holds for
the row-action, slash, shortcut-action and settings planes. What stands between it and
"better than desktop" is now concentrated in the recreate/notification architecture
(F-33-A/B/C/E) plus G61–G66. Census: 0 app FATALs, 0 app ANRs, one ~2 h 55 m boot, 774 ok
wires, 11 recreates. Artifacts: `/tmp/p33/` (rig.py, relay.sh/relay2.sh, netproxy.py,
hprof_*.py, shots/, atrest/, logcat-combined.log). Commits: this docs commit only. Nothing
pushed.

# Part BF — pass 34 (2026-11-07): the Android 16 (API 36) re-platform walk — every prior pass ran Android 11 — plus a census of the desktop's OWN browser mobile companion as the strictest on-par benchmark

Scope: all 33 earlier passes ran on an Android 11 (API 30) image, while the app targets API 36
and Ernest's phone runs a current Android. This pass replaced the emulator with **Android 16
(API 36)** and re-walked the app from a fresh install — so every modern-OS behaviour was
exercised for the first time: the notification runtime permission, the cached-app freezer and
background network block, predictive back, per-app language, the system Photo Picker, the
specialUse foreground service, the one-time camera grant, gesture navigation as the default,
and a real (virtual-scene) camera preview. On the desktop side, REA went to the one plane that
is literally the desktop team's own idea of a phone companion: the **browser-based mobile
shell** the desktop hosts for web remote control (G35), enumerated message-by-message against
what the native app sends and handles.

Rig: debug APK byte-identical `9084b920…` (versionCode 52 / 1.3.1, targetSdk 36), desktop
unchanged (3.14.5 / 3.14.5.7961, asar `99e280fb…`). **Emulator swap:** the Android 11 build was
deleted (system images `android-30;google_apis` + `android-30;aosp_atd` = 6.2 GB, AVDs
`zcode-pixel` 3.8 GB + `zcode-atd` 5.6 GB; free space 5.9 → 21 GB) and replaced by
`system-images;android-36;google_apis;arm64-v8a` rev 7 (build BE2A.250530.026.F3, 4.3 GB) on a
new AVD `zcode-a16` (1080×2340 @ 440 dpi, the S23 geometry of earlier passes, 2 GB guest RAM,
swiftshader, virtual-scene back camera). Fresh install (no restored data), fresh pairing, relay
generations 1→5. Census: 372,034 log lines, **0 app FATALs, 0 app ANRs**, 2,915 ok wires, 19
failed wires (all inside the freeze / zombie legs below).

## Part BF.2 — NEW defects (ordered by severity; every one reproduced and cited)

### F-34-D (P2) — voice dictation is dead on every device, and its error blames the device

The composer's + menu shows **Dictate** whenever `SpeechRecognizer.isRecognitionAvailable`
is true (`VoiceInput.kt:47-48`) — true on Android 16 here and on any phone with Google or
Samsung speech services. Tapping it calls `startListening` (`VoiceInput.kt:84`), and Android's
recognition service rejects the caller:
`RecognitionService: #startListening received from a caller without permission
android.permission.RECORD_AUDIO.` The app **does not declare `RECORD_AUDIO` at all** (manifest
grep: 0; `dumpsys package`: 0) and never asks for it, so `onError` fires and the composer shows
"Voice input isn't available on this device" (`composer_voice_unavailable`) — false: voice is
available, the app never asked for the microphone. Every earlier pass ran on an image without
a recognizer, where the item was hidden (pass 7: "gate-as-designed"), so the feature had never
run on a device. The parity ledger lists "voice input" as a phone-only WIN over the desktop;
today it is non-functional. Fix: declare `RECORD_AUDIO`, request it at the first Dictate tap
(the F-PERM direct-request pattern MainActivity already uses for the camera), and map
`ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_PERMISSIONS` to "Microphone permission needed" with a settings link. Pin: a
manifest-presence test + a Robolectric denied-permission path asserting the new copy.

### F-34-E (P2) — on Android 13+ the app never asks for notification permission, so a fresh install gets no approval alerts at all

On a fresh install `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` is `granted=false` and Android lists the app at
`importance=NONE`. Onboarding, pairing, the Tasks screen and the conversation never request
it; the only request site in the codebase is the Live-connection toggle
(`SettingsScreen.kt:947-968`). On the first background entry the broker re-posted three
attention items (`notify.repost` × 3) straight into a blocked sink
(`AndroidNotificationSink.kt:160`: `if (!manager.areNotificationsEnabled()) return`) — zero
notifications delivered, nothing told the user, and Settings → Notifications kept showing
Approval requests / Task finished / Connection lost all ON. This is pass 33's F-33-G
("blocked notifications look enabled"), but on Android 13+ it is not an edge case the user
created — it is **the default state of every new install**, which is why it is filed
separately at P2: a remote-approval companion that silently never alerts. Fix: request the
permission at the end of pairing (or at the first approval card) with a one-line rationale;
show a persistent "Notifications are off — Turn on" row on Tasks and in Settings while
`areNotificationsEnabled()` is false (the F-33-G remedy).

Context that makes this worse on Android 15+: without the Live-connection foreground service
the app has **no background delivery path at all**. Measured here: HOME at 14:30:47 → the
cached-app freezer froze the process (`isFrozen=true`) and the network policy blocked it
(`blocked=APP_BACKGROUND`) → `relay.lost` 7 s later; the second background lost the socket in
4 s; every reconnect attempt then timed out (10 s each) until the app returned to the
foreground. The Settings copy is honest about it ("Notifications are delivered while the app is
in use or when the Live connection is enabled. ZCode's relay offers no push service…"), but the
Live connection defaults OFF and is the last toggle in Settings. Recommendation: offer the
Live connection (with its battery note) in the same post-pairing step that asks for
notifications — that single step is what makes "approve from the shade" real on a modern phone.

### F-34-B (P2) — returning from the background can land in "Disconnected" for minutes: the reconnect budget is wall-clock and burns while the process is frozen

Sequence (all receipts in the pass log): HOME 14:36:32 → `relay.lost` 14:36:36 → reconnect
ladder relay-8…13, each attempt a 10 s connect timeout (network blocked) → the process freezes
**mid-attempt** (relay-13 started 14:37:36.897) → the user returns 14:41:12.887 →
`hub.foregroundTrigger` → `RelayTransport.reconnectNow()` (`RelayTransport.kt:846-863`): the
machine is RECONNECTING (not DEGRADED), so it only calls `requestImmediate()` and `recover()`,
and `recover()` is a single-flight no-op because the frozen loop still owns `recovering` →
the thawed attempt fails 34 ms later → the loop asks `ReconnectPolicy.nextDelayMs()`
(`ReconnectPolicy.kt:40-50`), which checks the 120 s budget **before** honouring
`immediateNext` — and the budget, measured with `System.currentTimeMillis` from 14:36:36, has
long expired → `RECONNECT_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED` → **DEGRADED at 14:41:13.872, in the foreground**,
and the loop quiesces by design. The app stayed "Disconnected" until 14:54:44 (13.5 min), when
a network flap re-triggered it; a user would have to find and tap Retry. The first background
of the session recovered in 1.46 s because the loop happened to be parked in a delay, not
mid-connect — so the outcome is timing-dependent, and on Android 15+ "mid-connect when frozen"
is the likely case because each background attempt lasts 10 s. Fix: a foreground entry is an
explicit user signal — `reconnectNow()` must open a fresh budget from RECONNECTING too (reset +
cancel/restart the parked loop), and `nextDelayMs()` should honour `immediateNext` before the
budget check. Pin: a ReconnectPolicy test with an injected clock jumping 5 min between attempts,
plus a transport test that `reconnectNow()` from RECONNECTING after budget expiry yields an
attempt, not DEGRADED.

### F-34-A (P2) — a notification tap onto the conversation that is already open stacks a duplicate; backing out of it leaves the remaining screen silently dead

With synth-task-1 open, the app backgrounded and a fresh approval arrived; tapping the
notification body at 15:10:03 delivered `zcode://task/synth-task-1#interaction=…` to the live
singleTask Activity, and `ZCodeApp.kt:204` ran `nav.navigate(Routes.conversation(link.taskId))`
with no `launchSingleTop` and no same-task check → a **second conversation entry for the same
task**. The predictive-back preview at 15:10:57 showed the identical conversation underneath.
Popping the duplicate ran `ConversationVmHolder.onCleared()` → `vm.onTeardown()` →
`hub.closeConversation(synth-task-1)` (`ConnectionHub.kt:828-840`) — and `openedSessions` is a
set keyed by task id, not a reference count, so the entry that stayed on screen lost its
subscription: `unsubscribeConversationV4 ok in 66ms`, `recovery.detached … (unsubscribed)`.
From then on the visible conversation is dead in the worst way: a send at 15:17:12 was
accepted on the wire (`sendConversationCommandV4 ok in 105ms`) but every update frame was
discarded — `gateway.drop :: session=synth-task-1 kind=ONLINE seq=5..5 / 6..6 / 7..7 (no
subscription record)` — so the composer cleared and the message and the agent's reply never
appeared (find-in-conversation: "No matches"). Control: Leave and re-open → snapshot subscribe →
find "p34dup1" = 1 of 2 (message and reply were there all along). Fix: navigate with
`launchSingleTop` and pop to an existing entry for the same task id; reference-count
`openedSessions` so only the last entry's teardown unsubscribes. Pin: a nav test (deep link to
the open task leaves exactly one conversation entry) + a hub test (two opens, one close → still
subscribed).

### F-34-C (P3, privacy) — the pairing camera keeps running after you leave the scanner

CameraX opened the camera at 14:19:42; the user left the scan screen for manual entry at
~14:23, completed pairing and reached the Tasks screen at 14:29:52 — and the camera, with the
QR-analysis use case, kept running until the app was backgrounded at 14:30:49
(`Camera2CameraImpl … Closing camera`) — about 7.5 minutes of invisible camera use, including a
minute on the paired Tasks screen. On a real phone the green camera privacy indicator stays lit
throughout. Cause: `QrScanner.kt:48-72` binds the use cases to the **Activity** lifecycle
(`bindToLifecycle(lifecycleOwner, …)` with the Activity) and never unbinds when the composable
leaves composition. Fix: `DisposableEffect { onDispose { provider.unbindAll() } }` (or bind to
the composable's own lifecycle owner). Pin: compose the scanner, remove it, assert the provider's
bound use cases are empty.

### F-34-F (P3, honesty) — the Live-connection notification says "Connected" while the app is disconnected

The ongoing foreground notification reads "Connected to MockBook — Live connection active — tap
to disconnect" (`LiveConnectionService.kt:86-87`, built once at service start). Through 14:44–
14:54 the transport was DEGRADED (in-app "Disconnected"), yet the shade kept saying Connected.
A user relying on the Live connection to receive approvals reads a false all-clear. Fix: have
the service observe the hub phase and update the notification text (Connected / Reconnecting /
Disconnected — tap to retry).

### Re-manifests on Android 16 (open defects, now confirmed on a modern OS)

- **F-33-A (P2)** zombie screen after recreate: dark-mode flip 15:29:54 → the retained screen's
  send now fails with `command.blockedOffline` (the old container's CommandCoordinator reads the
  destroyed transport) while its status line still says "Connected · Completed"; draft stuck.
  Control (leave + re-open, fresh entry): `sendConversationCommandV4 ok in 84ms`, frames 8–10
  delivered. Same root cause as BE.2 (`MainActivity.kt:128` per-Activity AppContainer;
  `ZCodeApp.kt:570-579` retained VM).
- **F-33-D (P3)** IME double inset: with the keyboard up and the pinned stack present the
  composer field is clipped and the attach/Send row is not painted; the accessibility tree keeps
  reporting the pre-keyboard positions (Send at y 1344–1476, behind the keyboard), so a tap there

  conversation row is visible while composing (the 48 dp timeline floor is not honoured).
- **F-33-F (P3)** clipboard read on every conversation open: `READ_CLIPBOARD` app-op times reset
  to 4 s after each open (32 min → 4 s → 4.6 s).
- **F-27-B (P3)** attachment thumbnail tap dead: mock.png tap = zero log lines, no viewer; at HEAD
  the `TimelineRow(…)` call at `ConversationScreen.kt:1047` still omits `onOpenAttachment`,

- **GAP-21-A (P3)** first-token `@re` = 0 `searchWorkspaceFiles` wires (11th repro); mid-text

## Part BF.3 — REA pass-34 dig: the desktop's own browser mobile companion, message by message

Method: the pass-24 flattened extraction of the unchanged asar (`/private/tmp/p24-asar`, digest
`99e280fb…` re-verified), byte-context reads of `out__main__index.js` (the remote-control host),
`out__renderer__assets__styles-C4MhEMbW.js` (the mobile shell and task home) and the IntlProvider
bundle (104 `webRemoteControl.*` keys, both locales).

### 1. Inbound message census — the phone sends 5 of the 10 messages the desktop handles

The host's `routePayload` switch (`out__main__index.js` ≈401,197) accepts ten mobile→desktop
`zcode_type`s:

| Message | What the desktop does with it | Native app |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bootstrap-request` | returns workspaces, tasks, `initialViewState` **and `mobileViewState`** | sends ✓ |
| `workspace-list-request` | workspace list | sends ✓ |
| `workspace-bridge-open` | opens the per-workspace RPC bridge | sends ✓ |
| `rpc-frame` / `rpc-frame-ack` | the RPC transport | sends ✓ |
| `mobile-view-state-update` | stores `{activeWorkspaceKey, activeTaskId, updatedAt}` + `deviceInfo {userAgent, viewport, updatedAt}` (`applyMobileViewStateUpdate`); surfaced in the desktop's remote-control status and replayed in the next bootstrap so the phone reopens where it was | **never sent** |
| `workspace-reconnect-request` | `e.reconnectWorkspace(windowId, workspaceKey)` → `workspace-reconnect-response` | **never sent** (the phone even lists `workspace-reconnect-response` among its control replies, `RelayTransport.kt:1189`) |
| `mobile-diagnostic` | writes the phone's connection diagnostics into the DESKTOP log: event, state/previousState, pairStatus, closeCode/closeReason/wasClean, failureReason/message, visibilityState, online, **hiddenDurationMs** | **never sent** |
| `platform-request` | dispatches one of 8 desktop platform methods (below) | never sent |
| `telemetry-report` | forwards a mobile telemetry event to the renderer telemetry | never sent — consistent with the phone's zero-analytics posture (a recorded phone win, not a gap) |

### 2. The remote-workspace hole (→ G67)

`workspace-bridge-open` for a remote (SSH/WSL/Docker) workspace whose connection is down throws
a plain error — "目标远程工作区尚未连接，无法创建 bridge，请先重连。" ("the remote workspace
is not connected; cannot create the bridge; reconnect first") — which the host's failure mapper
`FW()` turns into `reason: "unexpected-error"`. The browser shell detects the text
(`u8t`: "远程工作区尚未连接" / "请先重连") and offers Reconnect → `workspace-reconnect-request`.
The native app maps every reason outside its known list to PROTOCOL "Connection problem —
retrying" with `RECONCILE` (`ErrorMapping.kt:308-342`), so it retries a condition that only a
reconnect request can fix, and it has no way to send one. The phone decodes the workspace kind
(`BootstrapParser.kt:86`) but no UI uses `WorkspaceKind.REMOTE`.

### 3. The bridge-failure taxonomy vs the phone's mapping

The host emits `desktop-disconnected`, `workspace-closed`, **`unsupported-action`**
(remote workspace identity missing or mismatched) and **`unexpected-error`**, plus
`session-conflict` when the relay kicks the pairing; the companion's copy covers 12 failure
kinds. The phone maps nine reasons precisely; `unsupported-action` and `unexpected-error` fall
to the generic retrying copy. The desktop's own text for the first: "Web remote control mode can
only open workspaces that are already open in the current desktop window." Mobile slice: map both
reasons to honest copy, and route the "reconnect first" variant to G67's action.

### 4. Transport limits — why F-34-B and the freezer matter

- Disconnect grace: after the phone drops, the desktop keeps "phone connected" for **3 s**
  (`NW = 3e3`, `scheduleMobileDisconnectGrace`).
- Desktop→phone buffer while the phone is away: **50 payloads**, each batch **expires after 5 s**
  (`schedulePendingOutboundPayloadTimeout`, "dropped buffered outbound payloads"); overflow drops
  the whole buffer. So everything the agent emits while an Android 15+ phone is frozen is gone at
  the desktop; the phone's snapshot-replace recovery (`relay.recovered … snapshotReplace=true`,
  seen on every reconnect here) is the only reason nothing is lost — design validated.
- The desktop's own relay client: heartbeat every **10 s** (`pair_status_query`) with jitter,
  heartbeat-ack watchdog **30 s**, reconnect base **1 s**. Phone: same heartbeat verb, backoff 1 s →
  60 s cap, 120 s **wall-clock** budget (F-34-B).

### 5. The companion's task home vs the native Tasks screen (→ G69)

The browser task home (`WebRemoteControlMobileTaskHome`) offers: **Organize tasks — by workspace
/ Timeline**; **Sort by — Created / Updated**; **Collapse all workspaces**; Refresh; per-workspace
kind badges (Local / Remote / Conversation); a theme menu in the header; "Updated {time}" per
task; and it calls **`markTaskRead` when a task is opened** (`markTaskReadOnOpen`, only when the
task has `unreadAt`). The native app has none of organize / sort / collapse-all, shows no
workspace kind, and only offers a manual mark-read (`TasksViewModel.kt:281` setTaskUnread) —
opening an unread task on the phone leaves it unread on the desktop.

### 6. platform-request's 8 methods

`isDockerAvailable`, `listWSLDistros`, `listDockerContainers`, `listSSHConfigAliases` (remote
workspace authoring — the recorded B3 boundary of G41), `loadMcpFromUserDirectory`,
`saveMcpToUserDirectory`, `migrateLegacyCommonMcp` (MCP authoring — the G22/INV-9 read-only
viewer boundary) and **`createTempTextAttachment`** — the desktop's way to send a long paste as a
text file. Mobile slice of the last one: paste a long log as an attachment instead of a giant
message (P4, folded into G69's notes).

### New G rows

- **G67 (P3)** — remote-workspace reconnect: the phone cannot reconnect a disconnected remote
  workspace and misreports the bridge failure as a retrying connection problem. Mobile slice:
  detect the "reconnect first" bridge error, show "This remote workspace is disconnected —
  Reconnect", send `workspace-reconnect-request`, then retry the bridge.
- **G68 (P4)** — the phone reports nothing about itself to the desktop: no
  `mobile-view-state-update` (the desktop's status can't show which device is connected or what it
  is viewing, and the bootstrap can't restore the phone's last task) and no `mobile-diagnostic`
  (a support log on the Mac shows nothing about why the phone dropped — F-34-B would have been
  visible there as `hiddenDurationMs` + close code). Both are opt-in-able without analytics.
- **G69 (P4)** — task-home organisation: organize by workspace / timeline, sort created /
  updated, collapse all, workspace kind badges, and mark-read-on-open — the desktop's own mobile
  companion has all five.

## Part BF.4 — rig notes recorded for the next pass

- **Emulator is now Android 16**: AVD `zcode-a16` (`system-images;android-36;google_apis;arm64-v8a`
  rev 7). Boot: `emulator -avd zcode-a16 -memory 2048 -gpu swiftshader_indirect -no-audio
  -no-snapshot-load -no-snapshot-save -no-boot-anim -no-window -camera-back virtualscene` (60 s
  to `sys.boot_completed`). Gesture navigation is the image default (nav bar `[0,2274][1080,2340]`).
- **Pairing**: `/tmp/p34/typelink.py <resource-id> <link>` types in 12-char chunks with dump
  verification and self-resync (176/176, zero resyncs on API 36). Host-clipboard paste does not
  reach the guest with `-no-window`. The virtual-scene camera works, but aiming at a QR poster
  needs the emulator's gRPC pose control — the live QR-scan receipt stays rig debt.
- **The freezer is the default on API 36**: a backgrounded app is frozen within seconds and
  network-blocked (`dumpsys netpolicy … blocked=APP_BACKGROUND`); any background leg needs the
  Live-connection FGS on, or nothing happens.
- **IME**: `input keyevent 111` does not close Gboard here — use Back. With the keyboard up the
  accessibility tree reports the composer row at its pre-keyboard position; send with the IME's
  own action key (≈ 995, 2124) instead of tapping Send.
- **Per-app language**: the language picker needs the region sub-pick (简体中文 → 中国);
  `cmd locale get-app-locales / set-app-locales --locales ""` reads and resets it.
- **Clipboard probe**: `cmd appops get <pkg> READ_CLIPBOARD`.
- **Widget**: binding on the API 36 Pixel launcher was not automatable this pass (the picker list
  scrolls under `input motionevent`) — rig debt.
- Artifacts: `/tmp/p34/` (rig.py, relay.sh, typelink.py, send.sh, elfalign.py, findings.md, shots/,
  logcat-full.log, relay-gen1…5.log).

## Part BF.5 — pass-34 verdict and ledger delta

On Android 16 the companion installs, pairs, connects, renders edge-to-edge, honours per-app
language, uses the system Photo Picker, runs its specialUse foreground service correctly,
delivers approvals with working shade actions while that service is on, and answers every
interaction plane on the wire — 0 FATALs, 0 ANRs. The modern OS also exposed what Android 11
could not: **four P2s** (dead dictation, no notification permission ask on a fresh install, the
frozen-budget DEGRADED landing, the duplicate-entry dead screen), **two P3s** (camera left
running, a Live-connection notification that claims Connected), five re-manifests, four
smalls, and three new G rows (G67 remote-workspace reconnect, G68 mobile view-state/diagnostic
reporting, G69 task-home organisation) from the desktop's own browser companion.

**Fix-round opener order (supersedes BE.7):** F-34-D (manifest + runtime ask — the cheapest
fix of a whole feature) → F-34-E (notification ask + the off-state row, closes F-33-G with it) →
F-34-B (foreground opens a fresh reconnect budget) → F-33-A (process-scoped container; closes
F-33-B/C) → F-34-A (singleTop + reference-counted sessions) → F-33-D (one-line inset fix; re-pin
on painted Send + timeline floor) → F-27-B (the 3-line forwards) → F-34-C → F-34-F → F-33-E +
F-27-A → F-33-H → F-33-F → GAP-21-A (+ G65) → G67 → G64 → N-BC / N-BD / N-BE / N-BF smalls →
G68 + G69 → G48 + G51 → G60–G63, G66.

**On par / better:** the phone still beats the desktop's own browser companion on everything a
browser tab cannot do — shade notifications with Approve/Deny, the glance widget, launcher
shortcuts, per-app language through the OS, offline drafts with exactly-once delivery, and zero
telemetry — and matches it on bootstrap, bridge and RPC. What separates it from "better" on a
modern phone is now concrete: make notifications and the Live connection part of setup
(F-34-E), make the reconnect survive the freezer (F-34-B), fix the lifecycle class (F-33-A /
F-34-A), turn voice on (F-34-D), and add the companion's remote-workspace reconnect (G67).
Commits: this docs commit only. Nothing pushed.

# Part BG — pass 35 (2026-11-07): the armed-stack whole-app walk on Android 16 with every first-time receipt re-driven through the queue-mode composer, plus an i18n-namespace census of the desktop's settings pages — the pass that finally maps the desktop's AUTHORING planes against the phone's viewers

Scope: pass 34 re-platformed the emulator and walked the modern-OS surfaces; this pass walked
the app end-to-end on the same API 36 image with all 23 mock arms live, exercising every plane
that earlier passes receipted only in isolation — three seeded interaction cards answered in one
session, the git checkpoints/commit plane, the terminal consent gate driven live, the workflow
launch sheet, the mode/model chips, the full 18-section Settings inventory, the notification
permission ask through the Live connection, a shade approval under the foreground service, a
relay generation swap under the FGS, and process death. On the desktop side, REA stopped
enumerating single features and instead **censused the desktop's settings surface by i18n
namespace** (12,212 keys / 1,018 namespaces in `IntlProvider-B-44tSXQ.js`), which turns "the
desktop has more settings" into a page-by-page gap table — and it exposed planes no earlier
pass named: the rewind change-summary dialog, the hooks management page, MCP server authoring
with SSE + protocol-version pinning, a memory viewer, custom slash-command authoring, and a
usage-statistics model with streaks and error rates.

Rig: debug APK byte-identical `9084b920…` (versionCode 52 / 1.3.1, targetSdk 36), desktop
unchanged (3.14.5, asar `99e280fb…` re-verified). AVD `zcode-a16` (Android 16 / API 36,
1080×2340 @ 440 dpi). **Fresh install** (`pm clear` — the first clean-install walk since pass
34) → onboarding → paste-link pairing (178/178 chars with one self-resync after a runaway
first attempt) → Security setup → reduced security (no screen lock; the E7-skip papercut
re-seen) → seal → AUTHENTICATING → CONNECTING → CONNECTED. Relay generations 1→2 (gen 2
swapped while the app was backgrounded under the Live-connection FGS). Logcat was cleared
per leg (this image's buffer survives cold boots — see rig notes), so wire counts below are
per-leg receipts, not a session total. **0 app FATALs, 0 app ANRs** across the whole walk.

## Part BG.2 — defects and papercuts (new or re-manifested this pass)

### N-BG-1 (P3, usability; N-BF-3 worsened) — the three-group question card buries Submit behind a gesture that usually scrolls the wrong surface

With the mock's full seeded card (radio + radio + free text + checkbox group + second free
text) the pinned budget clips the card after the first question group; **"Send answers" sits
four inner scrolls deep**, and the first swipe attempts over the card scrolled the pinned
STACK to the next card instead of the card's inner content — the gesture boundary between
"scroll this card" and "cycle the pinned stack" is invisible and, in three of four attempts,
wrong. With the keyboard up (the free-text field focused) the card + queued strip + background
banner + shared-context chip consume the viewport and **not one pixel of the Submit is
reachable or hinted**. Pass 34's two-group card needed three scrolls; a third group pushes it
past the practical limit. Fix direction: cap the pinned card's inner scroll to the card
(fixed-height viewport with its own scroll), keep the stack cycle on the drag handle only,
and always render the submit row pinned at the card's bottom edge.

### N-BG-2 (P3, honesty) — refused channel calls are silent in the Git plane

Two live instances, both reproducible: the Commit dialog's **Generate** button
(`git.generateCommitMessage refused: fault.mock.unscripted` — mock debt, but the app side)
and the Changes/History tabs (`git.getChanges refused: fault.git.notAvailable`) produce **no
user-visible feedback** — the button does nothing, the tabs render empty, no snackbar, no
dialog, nothing in the log surface. On a real desktop a refused git call is a real failure the
user must see. The conversation plane surfaces refusals honestly (error cards); the Git plane
does not. Fix: route git-plane refusals through the same error-surface path (inline dialog
error row for Generate, an empty-state-with-reason for Changes/History). Mock debts to
unblock the rig: script `generateCommitMessage` and `getChanges` (or an arm to fault them
deliberately with UI assertions).

### N-BG-3 (P4, a11y/papercut) — the terminal consent gate's Switch is the only hit target, and Settings' custom switches are invisible to accessibility

The OptInGate row renders `Switch + Text("Enable terminal (view-only)")`; the TEXT is not
tappable — two taps on the label produced zero events and looked like a dead screen until the
Switch itself (left of the label, outside the label's bounds) was hit. In the same Settings
screen, the Live connection / Auto-reconnect / Terminal switches are custom `android.view.View`
nodes with no `checkable`/`checked` a11y state (the uiautomator tree shows plain Views; the
N-BC-1 unlabeled-switch family again). Fix: make the label toggle (onClick on the Row) and
expose `semantics { toggleable/selected }` on the custom switches.

### Re-manifests (open ledger, confirmed again on this build)

- **N-BE-4** — the hook-trust success notice "Trusted 2 hook(s) — the session continues."
  renders in the error-red family in dark theme (screenshot p35-trust-notice).
- **N-BD-1 (worse face)** — under the armed stack the slash palette renders **2 visible rows of

- **N-BF-2** — header "Connected · Completed" while the composer shows the running morph

- **N-BC-1** — Auto-send switch still unlabeled.
- **F-34-D** — Dictate present (recognition available on this image), tap hands off to the
  system voice IME path with no app-visible result; manifest still has **0 RECORD_AUDIO**

- **F-34-E** — the fresh install sat at `importance=NONE` for ~45 minutes of pairing, tasks,

## Part BG.3 — REA pass-35 dig: the desktop's settings surface, censused by i18n namespace

Method: the unchanged asar (`99e280fb…`) against the pass-24 flattened extraction; key census
from `out__renderer__assets__IntlProvider-B-44tSXQ.js` (**12,212 keys, 6,110 unique, 1,018
namespaces** — 6,106 keys were counted in pass 31; the delta is the backtick-key regex catching
more), plus byte-contexts in `out__renderer__assets__styles-C4MhEMbW.js` (the renderer body)
and `out__renderer__assets__src-mX5iVQ7P.js` (the shared schemas).

### 1. The desktop's settings pages vs the phone's 18 sections

`settings.*` namespaces with ≥4 keys resolve to **~20 desktop settings pages**: appearance,
automations, browser (44 keys — Chrome control: cookie/profile import with admin elevation,
clear cache/data, enable/disable control), commands (132), computerUse (28), hooks (120),
interfaceMode, mcp (204) + mcpServers (58), memory (73), migration (92), modelProvider (1198),
plugins (494), remoteSync, shortcuts (110 — keybindings), skills (246), subagents (172),
taskAutoArchiveDays, usage (286), workspaceFileSearch (30), zcodeInteractionBehavior. The phone
mirrors the viewer-type pages as read-only viewers (plugins, skills, MCP servers, subagents,
providers, bots) and its own mobile-native sections (notifications, live connection, privacy,
about) — but six desktop pages have **no phone surface at all** and four authoring forms have
no mobile slice.

### 2. New G rows (desktop planes no pass had named)

- **G70 (P3) — MCP server management** (`settings.mcp` 204 + `settings.mcpServers` 58 keys).
  The desktop authors servers in a form (name/command/args/env/headers/timeoutMs), supports
  **type stdio | sse**, pins **protocolVersion auto | legacy | modern**, accepts a full JSON
  config with paste hints, imports configs, syncs servers to remote workspaces
  (`settings.mcp.remoteSync` 38 keys), handles plugin-provided servers (28), OAuth (2) and a
  40-key failure taxonomy. The phone has the read-only list + status viewer (G22/INV-9). Mobile
  slice: the failure copy + status detail first; authoring is desktop-idiomatic and can stay
  desktop-only with an honest pointer.
- **G71 (P3) — hooks management page** (`settings.hooks` 120 keys). The desktop adds/edits/
  deletes hooks (event/matcher/matchAll/args/command/async/custom JSON with parse errors),
  groups them compatibility | configured | installed | legacy | plugins, and imports them.
  The phone surfaces hooks ONLY as trust-review cards in the conversation; Settings has no
  hooks row at all, so a phone user cannot even SEE what hooks a workspace runs after the
  trust decision. Mobile slice: a read-only hooks viewer (name/event/command/status) under
  Settings → workspace.
- **G72 (P3) — the rewind change-summary dialog** (`chat.changeSummary.rewindDialog` 19 keys
  + reason taxonomy 12; renderer mapper `bRt` at `styles-C4MhEMbW.js` @2905953 maps server
  reasons `bash_ignored / checkpoint_missing / checkpoint_unreadable / external_modified /
  file_read_failed / unsupported_checkpoint`). Before restoring, the desktop previews the
  rewind as **safe vs unsafe file lists with per-file reason attribution and an operation
  count**, and refuses cleanly (cannotApply / noSafeFiles / noUnsafeFiles). The phone's
  /rewind sends blind — and the preview that would feed this plane is exactly the
  `rewindPreviewProvider` param F-27-B drops at `ConversationScreen.kt:1047`. Fixing F-27-B
  delivers the data; G72 is the dialog on top of it.
- **G73 (P4) — automation editor depth** (`automations.*` 352 keys). The desktop editor has
  custom repeat rules (units minute/hour/day/month, byWeekday/byDate, ends/neverEnds, a month
  navigator), a maxRuns cap, **a per-automation model choice**, day-of-month + minute-level
  schedules, a recurring toggle, and create-via-chat. The phone (G29) authors a single
  time-of-day schedule + off-peak window, with History and row actions. Mobile slice: maxRuns
  and model on the existing editor; custom-repeat rules may stay desktop-only.
- **G74 (P4) — custom slash-command authoring** (`settings.commands` 132 keys: name/
  description/argumentHint/prompt form, delete, user vs plugin sources). The phone lists
  custom commands in the slash extras (the rig's cmd-deploy) but has no management surface.
- **G75 (P4) — memory viewer** (`settings.memory` 73 keys: files/index/memoryCount/localOnly/
  projectsDescription/refresh/fileChanged/fileDeleted/expand/collapse). The desktop has a
  memory (AGENTS.md-family) viewer with per-file state. The phone has zero memory surfaces —
  it cannot even view the AGENTS.md that /init creates.

### 3. Existing rows deepened

- **G60 (plan/usage plane)** deepens hard: `settings.usage` is 286 keys with a **daily chart**
  (max/peak/description), a **billing banner** (12), coding-plan metric/range/subject pickers,
  the **quota-reset countdown dialog with context reminder** (`codingPlan.quotaReset` 28), and
  the manual-claim banner + dialog with `failure.quotaExhausted`. Under it, the usage-stat
  schema in `src-mX5iVQ7P.js` @175598 carries **reasoningTokens / cacheCreationTokens /
  cacheReadTokens / cacheHitRate / totalSessions / totalTurns / toolCallCount / toolErrorRate /
  modelErrorRate / avgTimeToFirstTokenMs / avgTurnDurationMs / activeDays / currentStreakDays /
  longestSessionMs / longestStreakDays / peakDayTokens** — the phone's Usage viewer decodes the
  three quota bars and drops the rest.
- **G69 (task home)** — re-confirmed: the browser companion still has organize/sort/collapse-all
  and mark-read-on-open; the phone's per-workspace collapse receipt this pass narrows the gap to
  organize-by, sort, collapse-ALL, and mark-read-on-open.
- **Permission scoping (new small, folded into the approval-card ledger)**: the desktop's
  Allow-always/Deny-always carry **per-kind descriptions (command/file/generic)** and scope
  choices **allowForProject / allowForSession / cua.allowForProject** (`chat.permission.*` 64
  keys). The phone offers Allow once / Allow always / Deny with no scope choice — an
  always-allow on the phone has unclear breadth.
- **Context meter (new small)**: the desktop's contextUsage has a **token breakdown by
  category** (systemPrompt / systemTools / mcpTools / skills / messages / metaUserContext /
  toolPrompt) plus `cacheHitRate` and an inline compress action. The phone shows the percent
  bar only (the P4-smallest from pass 31 grows into this breakdown row).
- **Update plane (new small)**: the desktop dialog ships release notes + release date +
  skipVersion + autoDownloadAndInstall + cancelDownload + download progress + a ready-to-
  restart confirm, plus a **forceUpdate** blocking flow and post-update release notes. The
  phone's in-app update (F-UPDATE2, field-proven) shows none of that — a "what's new" row
  would be the cheap slice.
- **Queue parity confirmed, two niceties desktop-only**: the desktop has the same follow-up
  queue (`chat.queue.enqueue/edit/remove/paused.*`, `chat.followup.addToQueue/sendNow`) — but
  with drag-to-reorder (`chat.queue.drag`) and draft-conflict handling
  (`chat.queue.editDraftConflict/editRestoreFailed`). The phone's Move up/Move down buttons are
  the honest mobile equivalent.
- **Skills import (folded into G74's authoring note)**: `settings.skills.import` 42 keys —
  scan sources, copy | symlink modes, global | project scope, per-item importing/imported/
  failed. Read-only catalog + this import flow would cover the phone's skill needs.
- **Git branch switcher (small)**: the desktop's switcher carries a **blockedDialog** (branch
  switch blocked by dirty tracked/untracked files, with the file list and a resolve action)
  and a commit-identity-missing error. The phone creates/switches via the fork flow (pass 32
  ack fix) and has no blocked-state dialog.
- **Voice stays a phone-only plane**: zero dictation/speech surfaces in the desktop bundle
  (three greps, 0 hits) — which makes fixing F-34-D the difference between "the phone's voice
  is broken" and "the phone's voice is a genuine mobile-only win".

## Part BG.5 — pass-35 verdict and ledger delta

Every plane earlier passes verified in isolation now holds in one continuous armed session:
three interaction cards answered back-to-back, checkpoints + commit on the wire, the terminal
consent gate driven to a live stream, the workflow launch sheet, mode switches, the full
Settings inventory, the notification ask → grant → FGS → shade approval chain, a relay
generation swap under the foreground service (1.2 s recovery), and process death — **0 FATALs,
0 ANRs**. The new defects are two P3-class usability/honesty smalls (the buried question-card
submit, the silent Git refusals) and one a11y papercut; the open P2s (F-34-D voice, F-34-E
notification ask, F-34-B frozen budget, F-33-A zombie, F-34-A duplicate) all re-confirmed
unfixed at HEAD with pass-34 receipts standing. The REA census finally maps the desktop's
AUTHORING plane: six settings pages the phone cannot see at all (hooks management, memory
viewer, custom commands, browser control, keybindings, migration) and the MCP/automation/
usage/permission planes where the phone is read-only or shallow — filed as G70–G75 plus
deepened G60/G69 and four new smalls. The on-par verdict is unchanged and now precise: the
phone matches or beats the desktop on every RUNTIME plane (delivery, approvals, drafts, queue,
telemetry-free privacy, mobile-native surfaces), and the gap is concentrated in MANAGEMENT
surfaces — of which the honest mobile slices are G71 (a hooks viewer), G72 (the rewind preview
through the F-27-B fix), and the G60 usage depth.

# Part BH — pass 36 (2026-11-08): the armed-stack re-walk with eleven first-time legs, a Room/DataStore forensic layer pulled out from under the UI, and an REA dig into the interaction plane's own state object — the pass that finds the phone's quietest bugs (a setting it saves but can never read back, a two-day-old approval it keeps alive and re-notifies) and the desktop's five-minute answer deadline the phone has never been told about

Scope: pass 35 walked every plane in one armed session; this pass re-drove those legs on the same
build and image, then went where no pass had gone — **eleven first-time legs** (the Approvals
inbox as a destination, task search, automation History, the Usage viewer depth, the Skills and
Subagents viewers, the presentation-mode switch end-to-end, the attachment menu and the Sketch →
upload pipeline, the turn navigator from a scrolled-up position, the composer Stop morph's
recovery, a hook-review item in the `trusted_persistent` state, and an honest LMK-style process
death under the Live-connection FGS) — and, for the first time in the campaign, **pulled the app's
own storage off the device** (Room `zcode.db` + WAL, the DataStore protos) to check what the UI
claims against what the app actually persisted. Two of this pass's three new defects were found
that way and are invisible to any UI-only walk. On the desktop side, REA left the settings census
behind and decoded the **pending-interaction schema itself**, which surfaces the desktop's
question/approval auto-continue machine (a 5-minute default fuse with a visible countdown) that
the phone has never decoded; the three pages pass 35 named but did not adjudicate (browser
control, keybindings, migration) are closed out.

Rig: debug APK byte-identical `9084b920…` (versionCode 52 / 1.3.1, targetSdk 36 — an incremental
`:app:assembleDebug` over the docs-only HEAD reproduced it exactly); desktop 3.14.5, asar
`99e280fb…` re-verified. AVD `zcode-a16` (Android 16 / API 36, 1080×2340 @ 440 dpi), cold boot
(`-no-snapshot-load`; one System UI ANR dialog right after boot — rig noise, dismissed with
Wait). **No `pm clear`**: the stored pairing from pass 35 reconnected to a fresh relay generation
(gen 36, all 23 arms + `MOCK_INTERACTION_PUSH_MS=25000`) with no re-pair — and that surviving local
state is exactly what exposed F-36-B. Connection ids relay-1 → relay-6: five transparent reconnects
across emulator network flaps (`network.lost` / `network.available`) and the SIGKILL relaunch, none
user-visible. **0 app FATALs, 0 app ANRs.**

## Part BH.2 — NEW defects (ordered by severity; every one reproduced, root-caused, and cited)

### F-36-B (P2) — terminal-but-not-RESOLVED interactions never close: a stale approval from two days ago stayed in the Approvals inbox, was re-notified on background entry, and was answerable onto the live wire

**Receipt (Room forensics, `run-as … cat databases/zcode.db` + `-wal`):**

```
interactionId          kind        lifecycle  created (UTC)        resolvedAtMs
mock-p35-gen1-012a8f   PERMISSION  RESOLVED   2026-11-07 22:38:42  2026-11-07 23:27:05
mock-p35-gen2-90d324   PERMISSION  STALE      2026-11-07 23:27:04  NULL
mock-approval-1        PERMISSION  DISPLAYED  2026-11-08 00:53:23  NULL
mock-p31-gen36-eefe75  PERMISSION  RESOLVED   2026-11-08 00:53:47  2026-11-08 01:44:46
q-rig-1                USER_INPUT  RESOLVED   2026-11-08 00:58:31  2026-11-08 01:44:46
```

`mock-p35-gen2-90d324` is the push interaction from pass 35's relay-swap leg, staled by that
generation swap. It survived two days, an emulator cold boot, an `install -r`, and a new relay
generation, and at gen 36 it was still: (1) an **actionable Approvals-inbox card** — "Permission —
Bash · task Synthetic task · 2 h ago · Allow once / Deny" — counted in the bell badge (2);
(2) **re-posted as a permissions-channel notification** on background entry
(`notify.repost :: key=interaction:mock-p35-gen (background entry)` at 01:57:07 — under the
Minimal detail level that is a lock-screen "ZCode needs your approval" for nothing); and
(3) **answerable**: Allow once → `approvals.answer :: interaction=mock-p35-gen option=allowOnce`
→ **`sendConversationCommandV4 ok 33ms`** — a real command to the connected desktop for an
interaction id it never issued. Only that answer closed the row (badge 2 → 1).

**Mechanism — three sites compound:**
1. `InteractionCoordinator.updateLifecycle` (InteractionCoordinator.kt:804) mirrors
   `known.resolvedAtMs` into every upsert. The GAP-A2 fix made that non-null for RESOLVED only;
   STALE / EXPIRED / FAILED / CANCELLED persist with NULL even though `TERMINAL_MACHINE_STATES`
   (:795) already classes all four as terminal.
2. `InteractionDao.observeOpen` (Daos.kt:108-109) is `resolvedAtMs IS NULL` — so every
   non-RESOLVED terminal row is "open" to the inbox and to the notification repost.
3. `InteractionRepositoryImpl.sweep` (:79) TTL-drops only `resolvedAtMs != null` — a terminal-but-
   NULL row never ages out (only the 64-row cap could evict it). And after a process restart no
   in-memory machine exists for it, so the bootstrap's authoritative `pendingInteractions` (which
   did not list it) never reconciles it either — nothing in the app can ever close it.

**Fix shape:** stamp `resolvedAtMs` (or a terminal timestamp) for every `TERMINAL_MACHINE_STATES`
write; make `observeOpen` select `lifecycle IN (REQUESTED, DISPLAYED, SUBMITTING)`; TTL-sweep all
terminal lifecycles; on a session bootstrap, close stored open rows that the snapshot's
authoritative list no longer contains even when no machine exists; skip terminal ids in the
notification repost. **Pins against the real Room repo** (the GAP-A2 lesson — recording fakes
cannot see this): STALE write → `observeOpen` excludes; sweep drops a terminal row after TTL;
cold-start reconcile closes absent ids; repost skips terminal ids. GAP-A2 (P1, fixed) was the
RESOLVED half of this; this is the other four terminal states.

### F-36-C (P2) — G36's presentation mode can never be set to Office: the app saves "OFFICE" and reads it back as Coding

**Receipt:** Settings → Appearance → Presentation mode → Office → the dialog closes → reopen →
**Coding still selected** (twice; screenshots p36-presentation-dialog / -2), and the conversation
keeps the coding presentation (the Bash row still shows "echo synthetic"). The value WAS written:
`no_backup/datastore/preferences.pb` (pulled via run-as) holds field 15 =
`7a 06 4f 46 46 49 43 45` → **"OFFICE"**.

**Mechanism:** the writer stores the enum NAME — `.setInterfaceMode(mode.name)`
(DataStoreRepositories.kt:182) — while the reader runs the DESKTOP wire mapper —
`InterfaceMode.fromWire(if (hasInterfaceMode()) interfaceMode else null)` (:140-141 →
CoreModels.kt:271), which matches only `"office" | "general" | "concise"`. "OFFICE" falls through
to `else -> CODING`, so the setting round-trips to Coding forever: **the shipped G36 feature (vc51
Phase 4) is unreachable on device.** The only interfaceMode test is `InterfaceModeGateTest`
(features/conversation — gating on a supplied mode); no DataStore round-trip pin exists. This is
the second proto-mapping defect in this file after vc51 Phase 2's `interactionBehavior` builder
shadowing — the proto seam is the recurring blind spot.

**Fix:** write the wire spelling (`mode.name.lowercase()`) or read case-insensitively. Pin a
real-serializer round-trip: OFFICE → OFFICE, CODING → CODING, legacy "general" → OFFICE, garbage
→ CODING — and extend the same round-trip pin to every enum field in `AppPreferencesProto`.

### F-36-A (P3) — the turn navigator is buried under the jump-to-latest button whenever the timeline is scrolled up

Both floating buttons sit in the same corner of the same Box: the navigator's
`AnimatedVisibility(visible = navigatorQueries.size >= 2, Modifier.align(Alignment.BottomEnd))`
(ConversationScreen.kt:1087-1104) and jump-to-latest's `visible = !followBottom || !atBottom`, also
`Alignment.BottomEnd` (:1105-1126), composed later and so drawn on top. Scrolled up, the tree shows
`conversation_jump_latest (882,1538)-(1036,1692)` over `turnnav_open (904,1692)-(1036,1705)` — a
**13 px sliver**; screenshot p36-turnnav-after-taps shows only the ↓ button; four taps there all
went to jump-to-latest (the list snapped to the bottom) and no navigator sheet opened. At the
bottom (jump hidden) the navigator is 129 px and works — and the moment you use it (Jump to query 1
scrolls up) it is buried again for the next jump. The I2.5 comment's own promise — "ALWAYS
visible… discoverability is the finding's whole point" — fails exactly when navigating history.
Earlier receipts (lines 678, 833) exercised the sheet only from the bottom. **Fix:** stack the two
buttons (navigator offset above jump-to-latest by one button height + 8 dp) or put both in one
column; pin non-overlapping bounds when both are visible.

### N-BH-1 (P3, usability) — a message with only an attachment cannot be sent

Sketch → Done uploads the image (begin/chunk/commit all ok) and shows the chip, but with no typed
text the Send button stays **disabled** (`C---x-`) and a tap does nothing — the natural flow
(sketch → Done → Send) dead-ends until the user invents some text. The composer is internally
inconsistent: WriteComponents.kt:1035 computes
`hasDraftToSubmit = currentDraft.isNotBlank() || state.composerAttachments.isNotEmpty()` (the
GAP-A9 desktop contract counts attachments as submittable — it decides the Stop/Send morph), while
the Send button at :1058 is `enabled = state.draft.isNotBlank()`. Fix: gate Send on
`hasDraftToSubmit` (after confirming the `sendText` wire accepts an empty text with attachments).

### N-BH-2 (P4) — staged attachments do not survive process death; the text draft does

After `kill -9` + relaunch the composer restored the text draft from Room but the staged sketch
chip was gone. Because the upload is eager (committed at Done), the desktop is left holding an
orphaned upload and the user loses the chip silently. Persist the staged attachment references
with the draft (they are already server-side), or release the upload when the chip cannot be
restored.

### N-BH-3 (P4, a11y / clarity) — a trusted hook's disabled checkbox looks identical to an actionable one

In the hook-review card, a `trusted_persistent` item's checkbox is disabled by design, but it
renders exactly like the actionable ones, carries no content description, and has no "Trusted"
label beside it (only its Revoke button hints at the state). Two taps on the checkbox, one on the
row and one on the text produced no effect and no feedback; the uiautomator tree shows the boxes
as unlabeled CheckBoxes. Fix: replace the checkbox with a "Trusted" state chip (or add
`stateDescription` and a visible label) for non-actionable items.

### N-BH-4 (P4, a11y) — the presentation-mode dialog does not expose which option is selected

The options are clickable Rows wrapping `RadioButton(selected = …, onClick = null)` without
`Modifier.selectable(role = Role.RadioButton)` (SettingsScreen.kt ~1165-1180), so neither row
exposes a checked/selected state (uiautomator shows plain Views) — TalkBack cannot announce the
current mode. Fix: `selectable(selected, role = RadioButton)` on the Row; audit the theme dialog
for the same pattern.
